a105.speaker: Francisco Carvalho, President of the Praia Municipal Council (CMP)
a105.name: Francisco Carvalho
a105.title: President of the Praia Municipal Council (CMP)
a105.speech: Proposed to spread the amount received from the US embassy for the sale of the Club's land over 10 instalments, something the Tennis Club did not accept.

a105.speaker: Francisco Carvalho, President of the Praia Municipal Council (CMP)
a105.name: Francisco Carvalho
a105.title: President of the Praia Municipal Council (CMP)
a105.speech: Sparing with words, said only that if the Club had already gone to court, "it is up to the Court to decide and not for the Council to choose."

a105.speaker: An official of the Praia Tennis Club (anonymous)
a105.name: An official of the Praia Tennis Club (anonymous)
a105.speech: Said the mayor's reaction confirms the thesis that "the slowness of justice solves everything" ; "the prevailing idea in our society, that judicial proceedings take many years to be resolved, seems to be guiding the Council's behaviour."

a511.speaker: McHenry Venaani, PDM Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a511.name: McHenry Venaani
a511.title: PDM Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a511.speech: Put a question in parliament on the effects of the loss of grants from the US development agency USAID on the HIV/Aids and tuberculosis programmes.

a511.speaker: Dr. Esperance Luvindao, Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.name: Dr. Esperance Luvindao
a511.title: Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.speech: Answered in parliament that no formal assessment of the social and economic consequences of the abolition of US funding for vulnerable groups such as women, children and people with HIV/Aids has so far been carried out; she stressed that the Namibian government finances antiretroviral medicines (ARVs) entirely itself and that the ministry continues to supply all HIV and TB patients with state-financed medicines, procured through the health ministry's budget.

a511.speaker: Dr. Esperance Luvindao, Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.name: Dr. Esperance Luvindao
a511.title: Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.speech: Reported that targeted HIV testing for key populations and prevention programmes for young people are currently partly affected, and that the contracts of 23 staff in the voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) programme, including technical support for TB and HIV as well as NGOs funded by USAID, were cancelled; although supporting partners still provide targeted services, communities can also obtain these services in public health facilities, but the ministry needs additional funds to keep employing staff previously financed externally.

a511.speaker: McHenry Venaani, PDM Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a511.name: McHenry Venaani
a511.title: PDM Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a511.speech: Asked about new partnerships or alternative funding.

a511.speaker: Dr. Esperance Luvindao, Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.name: Dr. Esperance Luvindao
a511.title: Minister of Health (Namibia)
a511.speech: Stressed the urgent need to strengthen local financing, saying the ministry is working closely with the finance ministry to increase investment in health: "We are examining the reallocation of budget funds in favour of health services and ensuring that important programmes remain adequately financed," the minister said; through promoting corporate social responsibility initiatives and partnerships with private service providers, the ministry wants to create sustainable financing mechanisms to close the gaps created by external factors.

a606.speaker: Diamond TV
a606.name: Diamond TV
a606.speech: Has petitioned the Lusaka High Court to enter a default judgment against socialite Mutale Mwanza, citing her failure to appear or defend herself in a libel case; the television station is seeking damages and an injunction.

a606.speaker: Court documents (Lusaka High Court filings)
a606.name: Court documents (Lusaka High Court filings)
a606.speech: According to court documents, Diamond TV is seeking a declaration that Mwanza's statements are libelous, as well as damages for libel and damages for the mental anguish and stress caused to it.

a606.speaker: Mutale Mwanza, socialite
a606.name: Mutale Mwanza
a606.title: socialite
a606.speech: Allegedly referred to Diamond TV's Personality of the Year Awards (POTYAS) as "fraudulent" and "a scam" hosted by "hoes".

a705.speaker: Abebe Haile-Gabriel, FAO Assistant Director-General and Regional Representative for Africa (opinion piece)
a705.name: Abebe Haile-Gabriel
a705.title: FAO Assistant Director-General and Regional Representative for Africa (opinion piece)
a705.speech: Argued that social protection - comprising social assistance, social security and social welfare - plays an essential role in reducing poverty, alleviating hunger, improving food security, building resilience and contributing to productive livelihoods, and that it is urgent to expand the coverage and adequacy of social protection in Africa, particularly in rural areas. ; Wrote that expanding social protection in rural areas is not simply a safety net but a strategic investment in the transformation of agrifood systems, and that responsibility does not rest with national authorities alone: partnerships, knowledge sharing and sustained investment can open the way to a more prosperous, stable and equitable future for all.

a705.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a705.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a705.speech: Under the Global Partnership for Universal Social Protection, is committed to supporting member countries to extend the reach of appropriate national social protection systems and measures by 2030; through its Strategic Framework 2022-2031, FAO is committed to supporting African countries to extend the coverage, adequacy and comprehensiveness of social protection systems for rural populations, building on FAO's 'four betters': better production, better nutrition, better environment and better life, leaving no one behind.

a705.speaker: Statistics cited in the article (poverty, food security and social protection coverage figures)
a705.name: Statistics cited in the article (poverty
a705.title: food security and social protection coverage figures)
a705.speech: "The figures speak for themselves": 389 million people live in poverty in Africa, while 282 million people face a food security crisis; more than one billion Africans lack access to a healthy diet; only about 17% of the population in Africa is covered by at least one social protection benefit, rising to 27.1% for Africa's elderly population receiving an old-age pension.

a717.speaker: Lionel Zinsou, Prime Minister of Benin
a717.name: Lionel Zinsou
a717.title: Prime Minister of Benin
a717.speech: Revisited bilateral cooperation between the United States and Benin to stress that the first compact had shown convincing results for the national economy, citing the performance of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou as an example, and said he hoped the cooperation would continue.

a717.speaker: Lionel Zinsou, Prime Minister of Benin
a717.name: Lionel Zinsou
a717.title: Prime Minister of Benin
a717.speech: Dwelt on the importance of the second compact for Benin, accompanied by good-governance conditionality, in order to improve people’s daily lives through energy: “It is an important factor of development,” he reminded them. He also drew the board members’ attention to the task before them: “Benin is among the privileged countries with respect to the Compact II investment,” and urged them to succeed in their mission: “Doing so will make you fighters on the front line of the country’s development. Your responsibility is great in the face of this envelope destined for Benin for the happiness of our compatriots.”

a717.speaker: Lucy Tamlyn, U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a717.name: Lucy Tamlyn
a717.title: U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a717.speech: Praised the head of state’s commitment and the dynamism of cooperation between the two countries, and recalled that Compact II is an opportunity Benin must seize to improve the business climate and the daily lives of Beninese people.

a717.speaker: Fulbert Gero Amoussouga, Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
a717.name: Fulbert Gero Amoussouga
a717.title: Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
a717.speech: Insisted that together with his colleagues they grasp the significance of their appointment, and promised not to disappoint: “Our responsibility and our duty are great. They match the expectations of the people.” Speaking of Compact II, he praised it and revealed that it would contribute to improving the living conditions of several thousand of our compatriots, and said he hoped to count on everyone so that the set objectives are achieved.

a747.speaker: Head of State of Benin
a747.name: Head of State of Benin
a747.speech: Affirms the will to establish where responsibility lies (for the Tori-Bossito tragedy).

a747.speaker: Birago Diop, Senegalese writer
a747.name: Birago Diop
a747.title: Senegalese writer
a747.speech: Convinced us that: in Africa, the dead are not dead, the dead have never gone away.

a761.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a761.name: Marco Rubio
a761.title: US Secretary of State
a761.speech: Issued overnight an additional waiver for “life-saving humanitarian assistance” while Washington undertakes the 90-day review Trump initiated ; defined life-saving humanitarian assistance as core life-saving medicine, medical services, food, shelter, and subsistence assistance, supplies and reasonable administrative costs to deliver such assistance ; said the waiver will not apply to activities “that involve abortions, family planning conferences, administrative costs … gender or DEI (diversity, equity, and inclusion) ideology programs, transgender surgeries, or other non-life saving assistance,” according to a State Department memo sent to implementing partners and non-governmental organizations.

a761.speaker: Trump administration
a761.name: Trump administration
a761.speech: Says it is conducting the review to ensure the tens of billions of dollars worth of U.S. foreign assistance worldwide is aligned with Trump’s “America First” foreign policy and not a waste of taxpayer money.

a761.speaker: US State Department
a761.name: US State Department
a761.speech: Said on Wednesday that the pause in assistance stopped the provision of “condoms and other contraceptive services in Gaza”, clean energy programs for women in Fiji and family planning throughout Latin America, among other programs, saying that so far over $1 billion in spending “not aligned with an America First agenda has been prevented.” ; said in its statement on Wednesday that critical national security waivers had also been granted, including to ensure the protection of U.S. personnel overseas and enforce non-proliferation obligations, adding that exceptions have been reviewed and approved when needed within hours.

a761.speaker: Current and former USAID officials
a761.name: Current and former USAID officials
a761.speech: Said the move putting on leave about 60 career officials at USAID appeared designed to silence any dissent and raised concern about a lack of non-partisan leadership at the agency.

a761.speaker: USAID official (anonymous)
a761.name: USAID official (anonymous)
a761.speech: Speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, said “stop-work” orders issued on Monday for institutional support contracts resulted in 600 people being sent home and furloughed in the agency’s Global Health bureau.

a761.speaker: Public Health Institute (email to employees)
a761.name: Public Health Institute (email to employees)
a761.speech: Sent an email to its employees late on Tuesday saying their employment has been terminated as a result of a stop-work order.

a764.speaker: Captain Rama Balde, communications officer of the Directorate General of the National Police of Guinea
a764.name: Captain Rama Balde
a764.title: communications officer of the Directorate General of the National Police of Guinea
a764.speech: Declared that the Directorate General of the National Police is continuing its campaigns against organised crime and that it is in this framework that the Central Police Station of Dubreka carried out sweep operations in crime-prone areas within its jurisdiction, namely Dondolikhoure, Fofomere and Tobolon. “This new raid on the various dens made it possible to apprehend 12 alleged delinquents, who were holders, sellers and consumers of drugs. It is a vast clean-up operation aimed at ridding the town of delinquents and establishing a climate of peace and security,” she explained ; she went on to indicate that during these patrols in the criminals’ nests, a significant quantity of narcotics and other psychotropic substances were seized: 51 balls and half a kilogramme of Indian hemp, 4 pairs of scissors and a kitchen knife.

a764.speaker: Mamadou Camara, public prosecutor at the Court of First Instance (TPI) of Dubreka
a764.name: Mamadou Camara
a764.title: public prosecutor at the Court of First Instance (TPI) of Dubreka
a764.speech: Assured the population that his office would take the necessary measures so that these alleged offenders may serve as an example: “We will spare no effort in the prosecution of these individuals in order to seek exemplary sentences, very rigorous sentences against them so that they cannot reoffend and so that other people who have taken that path will be deterred,” he promised.

a1348.speaker: Ibrahim Matola, Malawi Minister of Energy
a1348.name: Ibrahim Matola
a1348.title: Malawi Minister of Energy
a1348.speech: Announced that the first tankers of fuel are expected to arrive in Malawi on Thursday, January 9, and that the loading of road tankers is expected to commence on Monday, January 6th with a capacity to load up to 80 tankers per day. ; "A total of 1,409 truck loadings shall be required to bring the entire fuel volumes into Malawi. Both Malawian and foreign transporters have been engaged to ensure efficient and timely delivery of these volumes. In the meantime, fuel from contracted suppliers for National Oil Company of Malawi (NOCMA), Petroleum Importers Limited (PIL) and other licensed importers continues to flow into the country." ; "The emergency fuel procurement aims at supplementing the normal fuel imports by NOCMA, PIL and other licensed importers which have faced challenges in accessing fuel import financing leading to the current fuel shortages. This consignment has been procured under the Kenya bilateral arrangement between the Government of the Republic of Kenya and the Government of the Republic of Malawi using Kenya's existing G-to-G arrangement with Abu Dhabi while Malawi works to put in place its own G-to-G fuel supply framework with Gulf countries. The vessel carrying this maiden consignment, MT High Freedom, arrived at the port of Tanga in Tanzania on 29th December 2024. The fuel was tested by SGS on 31st December 2024 and was duly certified as meeting Malawi's technical specifications. The Ministry wishes to assure the general public that the Government and all relevant stakeholders are working tirelessly to address the fuel supply challenges the country has faced in recent months."

a1348.speaker: ZBSNews
a1348.name: ZBSNews
a1348.speech: Reported yesterday from Tanga Port in Tanzania that the Minister, officials from NOCMA and Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA) had an interface with authorities Gulf Bulk Petrolium (GBP) at the port.

a1348.speaker: Ibrahim Matola, Malawi Minister of Energy
a1348.name: Ibrahim Matola
a1348.title: Malawi Minister of Energy
a1348.speech: Was quoted as saying the decision to use Tanga Port in the procurement of the emergency fuel supply has been necessitated by heavy congestion in Dar es Salaam, Beira and Nacala ports. Matola told ZBSNews that using the usual ports would have resulted in Malawi receiving the fuel in the next months which could have created pressure and switching to Tanga Port is a decision that is a game changer in stabilising the availability of fuel in Malawi and its fuel reserve. He added that the country has 60 million liters capacity in all its three strategic fuel reserves and has emphasised that the government is not abandoning the open-tender fuel procurement deals.

a1348.speaker: Ibrahim Matola, Malawi Minister of Energy (Facebook post)
a1348.name: Ibrahim Matola
a1348.title: Malawi Minister of Energy (Facebook post)
a1348.speech: Pledged his focus remains clear to ensure consistent fuel availability nationwide — emphasising that under his watch, the Ministry "will work tirelessly to ensure that fuel shortages and queues become a thing of the past". He also pledged on building a more resilient energy sector for all Malawians by "expanding rural electrification, diversifying our energy mix, attracting investment in renewable energy, and strengthening our power infrastructure". He added that his reappointment as Energy Minister reflects not just trust in his leadership, but a commitment to continuity in the nation's energy transformation agenda. ; "In my previous tenure, we made significant strides in expanding our power generation capacity, improving distribution networks, and implementing sustainable solutions to stabilize our fuel supply chain."

a1348.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a1348.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a1348.title: President of Malawi
a1348.speech: In his address on New Year's Day, pledged that configuration of his Cabinet will work harder than ever to make Malawians' lives better this year and beyond.

a1384.speaker: US State Department
a1384.name: US State Department
a1384.speech: The United States said it would revoke Colombian President Gustavo Petro's visa after he took to New York's streets in a pro-Palestinian demonstration and urged U.S. soldiers to disobey President Donald Trump's orders. "We will revoke Petro's visa due to his reckless and incendiary actions," the State Department posted on X.

a1384.speaker: Gustavo Petro, Colombian President
a1384.name: Gustavo Petro
a1384.title: Colombian President
a1384.speech: Addressing a crowd of pro-Palestinian protesters outside the U.N. headquarters in Manhattan, called for a global armed force with the priority to liberate Palestinians, adding, "This force has to be bigger than that of the United States." ; "That's why from here, from New York, I ask all the soldiers of the army of the United States not to point their guns at people. Disobey the orders of Trump. Obey the orders of humanity," Petro said in Spanish.

a1384.speaker: Gustavo Petro, Colombian President
a1384.name: Gustavo Petro
a1384.title: Colombian President
a1384.speech: Hit out at Trump in his speech to the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday, saying the U.S. leader was "complicit in genocide" in Gaza and calling for "criminal proceedings" over U.S. missile attacks on suspected drug-running boats in Caribbean waters.

a1384.speaker: Gustavo Petro, Colombian President
a1384.name: Gustavo Petro
a1384.title: Colombian President
a1384.speech: On refusing to accept military flights carrying deportees in Trump's immigration crackdown, said his country's citizens were being treated like criminals.

a1384.speaker: Gustavo Petro, Colombian President
a1384.name: Gustavo Petro
a1384.title: Colombian President
a1384.speech: Came to office in 2022 promising agreements with armed groups but pivoted last year, pledging to tame coca-growing regions with massive social and military intervention.

a1384.speaker: Petro's office and Colombia's foreign ministry
a1384.name: Petro's office and Colombia's foreign ministry
a1384.speech: Did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

a1384.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a1384.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a1384.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a1384.speech: Addressing the assembly on Friday, denounced Western countries for embracing Palestinian statehood, accusing them of sending the message that "murdering Jews pays off."

a1384.speaker: Gaza health authorities
a1384.name: Gaza health authorities
a1384.speech: According to Gaza health authorities, Israel's military campaign in Gaza has killed more than 65,000 Palestinians and displaced the entire population of the narrow enclave.

a1384.speaker: Israel
a1384.name: Israel
a1384.speech: Angrily denied the charge of genocide, saying the war is in self-defense.

a1384.speaker: Trump administration
a1384.name: Trump administration
a1384.speech: Said it would not give Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to travel to New York.

a1384.speaker: Office of Mahmoud Abbas, Palestinian Authority President
a1384.name: Office of Mahmoud Abbas
a1384.title: Palestinian Authority President
a1384.speech: Said at the time that his visa ban violated the 1947 U.N. headquarters agreement, under which the U.S. is generally required to allow access for foreign diplomats to the U.N.

a1384.speaker: Washington (US government)
a1384.name: Washington (US government)
a1384.speech: Has said it can deny visas for security, extremism and foreign policy reasons.

a1384.speaker: Washington (US government)
a1384.name: Washington (US government)
a1384.speech: Trump this month put Colombia on a list of countries that Washington says have failed to uphold their counter-narcotics agreements, blaming Colombia's political leadership.

a1392.speaker: Thomas Nyarko Ampem, Deputy Minister Designate for Finance of Ghana
a1392.name: Thomas Nyarko Ampem
a1392.title: Deputy Minister Designate for Finance of Ghana
a1392.speech: Stated that the sudden withdrawal of USAID funding should serve as a wake-up call for Ghana to start planning for self-sufficiency: "It is important that we begin to plan our lives without aid and see what we can do for ourselves." ; Speaking during his vetting before the Appointments Committee, he explained that foreign aid to Ghana has been declining over the years and is likely to cease entirely in the near future. He noted that before USAID withdrew its funding, Ghana had been expecting approximately $150 million to support key sectors such as health, education, and the economy. He emphasised that the timing of the withdrawal was fortunate, as the Ministry of Finance was in the process of preparing the 2025 budget, and added that the President had already issued a directive to seek alternative funding sources to address the shortfall: "It happened at a time, fortunately we are in the process of preparing the 2025 budget. So I am sure the Minister would be able to make provision to bridge the gap."

a1400.speaker: Humanitarian assistance experts
a1400.name: Humanitarian assistance experts
a1400.speech: Have warned the agency's demise will harm vulnerable people and weaken US soft power.

a1400.speaker: USAID (notice on its website)
a1400.name: USAID (notice on its website)
a1400.speech: Said all USAID employees, with the exception of "designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and/or specially designated programs", will be placed on "administrative leave globally" from 11:59pm EST on Sunday; the process of laying off about 1,600 US-based personnel will take place concurrently. "Individuals that are impacted will receive specific notifications on February 23, 2025, with further instructions and information about their benefits and rights." ; "Designated essential personnel who are expected to continue working will be informed by Agency leadership February 23, 2025, by 5 pm EST [22:00 GMT]." ; "For overseas personnel, USAID intends a voluntary Agency-funded return travel program and other benefits." ; "USAID is committed to keeping its overseas personnel safe. Until they return home, personnel will retain access to Agency systems and to diplomatic and other resources. In the coming week, we will provide details on how to retrieve personal items from the former USAID workspaces and return government issued devices."

a1400.speaker: USAID (earlier notice sent to employees)
a1400.name: USAID (earlier notice sent to employees)
a1400.speech: Had said about 2,000 US-based jobs would be eliminated. No reason was provided for the discrepancy.

a1400.speaker: US judge (ruling on Friday)
a1400.name: US judge (ruling on Friday)
a1400.speech: Cleared the way for the Trump administration to push ahead with its plans to call back thousands of USAID staffers from overseas within 30 days.

a1400.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1400.name: Elon Musk
a1400.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a1400.speech: Has called USAID a "criminal organization" and a "viper's nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America"; Musk and other Trump allies have claimed the agency is rife with waste and fraud, and pursues a liberal ideological agenda that is outside the scope of its mission.

a1400.speaker: Former USAID officials and humanitarian workers
a1400.name: Former USAID officials and humanitarian workers
a1400.speech: Have decried Trump's move, warning that the demise of the aid agency will harm millions of vulnerable people worldwide and weaken US soft power.

a1400.speaker: Marcia Wong, former deputy assistant administrator for USAID's Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance
a1400.name: Marcia Wong
a1400.title: former deputy assistant administrator for USAID's Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance
a1400.speech: Said on X: "Eliminating US unique response capacity of crisis experts who help contain disease outbreaks, stabilise displaced populations – a shortsighted, high risk and frankly, stupid act."

a1458.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.name: Jean Kaseya
a1458.title: Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.speech: Said at the bi-weekly media webinar news conference on Thursday that millions of lives across the continent are at risk due to abrupt cuts in US and European development aid, threatening to reverse decades of progress in global health; warned that as the US Congress gears up to debate the reauthorisation of PEPFAR on 25 March, the fate of millions of Africans remains uncertain, and described the situation as a "total disaster" for the continent's health sector ; said that 30 per cent of Africa's health expenditure comes from Official Development Assistance (ODA) and that in 2025 ODA funding has been slashed by 70 per cent, dropping from $81 billion to just $25 billion.

a1458.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.name: Jean Kaseya
a1458.title: Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.speech: "Beyond HIV/AIDS, the funding crisis comes amid a surge in disease outbreaks across Africa—up 41 per cent in the past two years." ; "In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the loss of USAID funding has disrupted Mpox testing, leading to a 16 per cent drop in confirmed cases not because the outbreak is under control, but due to a lack of resources to track it. The turnaround time for testing has also increased in many regions due to logistical challenges."

a1458.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.name: Jean Kaseya
a1458.title: Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.speech: Said the aid cuts threaten to undo 20 years of progress in maternal and child health, infectious disease control, and poverty reduction, and that with donor funding disappearing entire health systems could collapse and millions more Africans could be pushed into extreme poverty: "Africa CDC projects that 39 million people will be driven into poverty as a direct result of these funding cuts."

a1458.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.name: Jean Kaseya
a1458.title: Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.speech: Said that health financing remains a persistent challenge: "Only two African countries, Botswana and Rwanda, meet the Abuja Declaration's commitment to spend 15 per cent of GDP on health and only 16 countries have national health financing plans in place"; noted that without external funding, many nations are struggling to keep their health services afloat.

a1458.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.name: Jean Kaseya
a1458.title: Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a1458.speech: Said he has been meeting with ministers and the African Union to push for increased domestic investment in health and explore "blended financing" strategies involving the private sector: "One innovative proposal involves leveraging the $95 billion in annual remittances from the African diaspora, potentially through a taxation model to fund healthcare initiatives" ; "With limited time to act, I will be meeting with members of the Trump administration, PEPFAR officials, and US lawmakers to make the case for continued aid."

a1458.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1458.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1458.speech: Said the Trump administration's decision to pause US foreign aid has "substantially disrupted" supply of HIV treatments in eight countries — Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria and Ukraine — which could soon run out of these life-saving medicines; said the US has a "responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it's done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding"; said funding shortages could also force 80 per cent of its supported essential health care services in Afghanistan to close, and that as of 4 March 167 health facilities had shut down due to funding shortages, with over 220 more facilities at risk of closing by June without urgent intervention.

a1458.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a1458.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a1458.speech: Reports that President Donald Trump had in January issued an executive order declaring a 90-day pause to all foreign assistance.

a1585.speaker: Assmang (joint venture between African Rainbow Minerals and Assore), notice to unions
a1585.name: Assmang (joint venture between African Rainbow Minerals and Assore)
a1585.title: notice to unions
a1585.speech: said in a notice to unions seen by Reuters on Tuesday that the closure of the mine could result in the loss of 688 jobs ; said ArcelorMittal South Africa had, in what Assmang called "an unexpected turn of events", confirmed in June that it would not sign a three-year contract with Beeshoek despite earlier indications that it would do so ; "Moving forward, Beeshoek proposes to discuss with the unions the potential closure of Beeshoek" ; "The mine has only one significant customer, ArcelorMittal South Africa. The customer is not willing and has declined concluding any long-term contract with Beeshoek mine," adding that several alternatives, including exports, had been considered but ultimately deemed unviable.

a1585.speaker: ArcelorMittal South Africa
a1585.name: ArcelorMittal South Africa
a1585.speech: did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

a1585.speaker: ArcelorMittal South Africa
a1585.name: ArcelorMittal South Africa
a1585.speech: has said that talks with the government, labour representatives and utilities companies over its deferred closure of the loss-making long steel plants in Newcastle and Vereeniging have, so far, not produced a solution.

a1585.speaker: Trade union Solidarity
a1585.name: Trade union Solidarity
a1585.speech: said Assmang had initiated the process to lay off the entire staff at the mine.

a1585.speaker: Adele Rossouw, Solidarity's organiser for the mining sector
a1585.name: Adele Rossouw
a1585.title: Solidarity's organiser for the mining sector
a1585.speech: "Due to the fact that they do not export, and since their only client can no longer buy from them, the worst possible option is now being considered," said in a statement.

a1719.speaker: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a1719.name: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a1719.speech: According to OPEC Secretariat calculations, the price of the OPEC basket of 12 crudes stood at $74.90 a barrel on Thursday, October 3, 2024, compared with $74.62 the previous day.

a1760.speaker: United States government
a1760.name: United States government
a1760.speech: Said it would cut $50 million in annual aid to Zambia's health sector because the government had failed to stop "systemic theft" of donated medicines and medical supplies.

a1760.speaker: Michael Gonzales, U.S. ambassador to Zambia
a1760.name: Michael Gonzales
a1760.title: U.S. ambassador to Zambia
a1760.speech: Said in a statement that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration is finalising a broader review of its foreign aid, but the cut for Zambia is "wholly separate from that process." ; "I am disappointed to share publicly today that since 2021 we have uncovered systemic theft of life-saving medicines and other products that were intended for free for the Zambian public," adding medicines stolen included antiretroviral drugs used to treat HIV.

a1760.speaker: Michael Gonzales, U.S. ambassador to Zambia
a1760.name: Michael Gonzales
a1760.title: U.S. ambassador to Zambia
a1760.speech: Said he had recommended to Washington that the U.S. continue to procure and deliver lifesaving medicines and medical supplies to Zambia until January 2026 to provide time for the government to develop a transition plan; said that after January, the U.S. will still offer technical and logistics assistance to support humanitarian activities and prevent drug resistance and disease transmission.

a1760.speaker: Zambia's health ministry (statement)
a1760.name: Zambia's health ministry (statement)
a1760.speech: Responded in a statement acknowledging the U.S. ambassador's concerns and said recurrent theft of medicines was a "persistent challenge" dating back to before 2021. The ministry said that after he was alerted to the issue Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema commissioned an independent forensic audit of the entire medicines supply chain, and that a number of officials found to have been involved had been removed from office or suspended, while others were arrested and are set to appear in court. "We want to assure the public that Zambia currently maintains sufficient stocks of essential medicines, including antiretroviral, antimalarial, and other critical drugs, with no immediate risk of shortages."

a2011.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC), provisional figures
a2011.name: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a2011.title: provisional figures
a2011.speech: Provisional figures released by the MEC indicate that Mutharika, representing the Democratic Progressive Party, has secured about 66 percent of valid votes counted so far, while Chakwera, the Malawi Congress Party candidate, trails with just 24 percent, with results from a handful of districts still pending.

a2011.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a2011.name: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a2011.speech: Has pledged transparency and accuracy in its final count amid heightened scrutiny following the annulment of Mutharika’s 2019 victory due to irregularities.

a2011.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and former president Bakili Muluzi
a2011.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and former president Bakili Muluzi
a2011.speech: Have publicly urged Chakwera to accept the outcome and congratulate Mutharika.

a2011.speaker: Billy Gamah, Malawi Council of Churches chairperson
a2011.name: Billy Gamah
a2011.title: Malawi Council of Churches chairperson
a2011.speech: Said the remaining tallies are unlikely to reverse the trend, describing a concession as “an act of statesmanship” that would promote calm and maturity among supporters ; “We believe that conceding early, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace and help the nation move forward without violence or unnecessary tension,” Gamah told local media.

a2011.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former president of Malawi
a2011.name: Bakili Muluzi
a2011.title: former president of Malawi
a2011.speech: Echoed the sentiment in an interview with the privately owned Zodiak Broadcasting Station, saying Chakwera should “allow the country to move on” and reminding him that “there is life after State House.”

a2075.speaker: Local authorities of Nampula province
a2075.name: Local authorities of Nampula province
a2075.speech: Announced on Wednesday that at least 71 people died of tuberculosis in the first half of this year in Nampula province, a year-on-year increase of 5%.

a2075.speaker: Jaime Miguel, head of the public health department at the Provincial Health Directorate of Nampula (cited by Noticias ao Minuto)
a2075.name: Jaime Miguel
a2075.title: head of the public health department at the Provincial Health Directorate of Nampula (cited by Noticias ao Minuto)
a2075.speech: "There are 71 deaths this year, in the first half. If we compare with the same period of the previous year, we had a slight increase of 5%, because at the same time last year we recorded close to 60 cases." ; According to him, the province recorded 6,935 tuberculosis cases in the same period last year, and the authorities are asking the population to redouble prevention efforts; he stated that cases have a higher incidence in the districts of Nampula, Mogovolas, Erati and Liupo.

a2075.speaker: Jaime Miguel, head of the public health department at the Provincial Health Directorate of Nampula
a2075.name: Jaime Miguel
a2075.title: head of the public health department at the Provincial Health Directorate of Nampula
a2075.speech: Said one of the causes of the increase in cases is the weak provincial coverage in screening and treating tuberculosis cases in communities, especially with the departure of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), which supported local organisations in the fight against the disease: "We have some communities that do not have coverage by activists, and, given our ratio of health technicians, health units and population, there are people who travel kilometres to reach a health unit" ; "the fact that we are unable to follow up cases in the communities contributes, because the cases that arrive at health units are severe cases."

a2075.speaker: Mozambican health authorities
a2075.name: Mozambican health authorities
a2075.speech: Pointed to the lack of funding as one of the causes of the increase in cases of the disease in the country, in recently released data indicating 48,000 tuberculosis cases in the first half of this year.

a2075.speaker: Ivan Manhica, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a2075.name: Ivan Manhica
a2075.title: Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a2075.speech: Said last July: "Mozambique continues to face a high burden of this disease, often associated with HIV, seriously affecting mainly the most vulnerable populations."

a2075.speaker: US Government
a2075.name: US Government
a2075.speech: Announced on 1 July the definitive closure of USAID, founded in 1961 with the aim of providing international humanitarian support, with significant funding in the health area in Mozambique.

a2075.speaker: Development Aid from People to People Association (ADPP)
a2075.name: Development Aid from People to People Association (ADPP)
a2075.speech: According to ADPP, more than 108,000 people have received tuberculosis treatment since 2019 in 50 districts of the provinces of Zambezia, Sofala, Tete and Nampula; and between 2019 and 2024, of the total of 108,242 cases notified and treated in the country, 10,547 were children.

a2175.speaker: Presidency of South Africa
a2175.name: Presidency of South Africa
a2175.speech: announced on Monday that President Cyril Ramaphosa will make a State visit to Switzerland on 29 and 30 October in order to strengthen cooperation in the fields of trade, science and youth development.

a2175.speaker: Vincent Magwenya, spokesperson for the South African Presidency
a2175.name: Vincent Magwenya
a2175.title: spokesperson for the South African Presidency
a2175.speech: said the visit will emphasise efforts to increase investment, skills development and scientific collaboration: "One of the main focuses of the visit will also be the promotion of a cooperation framework for youth aimed at promoting training and capacity building in order to equip young people with the skills required in the modern economy."

a2175.speaker: South African Revenue Service data
a2175.name: South African Revenue Service data
a2175.speech: values bilateral trade at 18.2 billion rand (about 1.1 billion dollars) in 2024.

a2175.speaker: Swiss figures
a2175.name: Swiss figures
a2175.speech: taking gold exports into account, indicate volumes reaching 159.5 billion rand, positioning Switzerland as the country's sixth-largest trading partner.

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin (address to the nation)
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin (address to the nation)
a2177.speech: said the vote reflects the will and determination of the Beninese people, through their national representation, to ensure better governance and better management of the country's resources, which will strengthen democratic culture, respect for public property, the obligation of results and accountability; the law thus constitutes "a privileged instrument for the fight against bad governance, the embezzlement of public funds and illicit enrichment" ; "the vote of this law gives hope back to our people and constitutes a privileged instrument in the fight against impunity, bad governance, embezzlement of public funds, illicit enrichment, injustice, and so on."

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: stressed that with the vote of this law Benin is among the rare countries possessing anti-corruption legislation, and is now on the short list of African and ECOWAS countries with such laws, being one of the eight countries of the sub-region to have ratified the anti-corruption protocol.

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: recalled the various actions carried out since he came to power in 2006 to defeat corruption: the creation of the General State Inspectorate (IGE), the appointment of ministry Inspectors General by the President rather than by ministers, the appointment of internal auditors in public enterprises, the establishment of a hotline at the Presidency of the Republic, the creation of the Observatory for the Fight against Corruption (OLC), the setting up of the national structure of the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM), the drawing-up of a price reference framework in the public administration, the cleaning-up of public procurement procedures and the reforms under way at the Port of Cotonou including the Single Window and the new-generation Import Verification Programme (PVI).

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: addressed his "warm and lively congratulations" to the honourable deputies of the National Assembly for their courage, and invited the deputies of the sixth legislature to join in this noble and exalting republican mission, saying he had no doubt about the determination of the national representation to continue the work of strengthening the democratic process.

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: associated himself with citizens of the Islamic community to wish them a good Ramadan feast, saying the nation is grateful for the prayers they sent up to the Creator to implore his mercy on the country.

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: assured that he remains faithful to his commitments and that the reforms are only beginning, others will inevitably follow, since they all contribute to restoring the spiritual, ethical and moral values that were once the foundation of the Republic; he asked for citizens' commitment and their readiness for the sacrifices implementation will require.

a2177.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a2177.name: Boni Yayi
a2177.title: President of Benin
a2177.speech: reassured compatriots in towns and countryside that, after verification of the new law's conformity with the Constitution and its promulgation, his government will ensure both the adoption of implementing decrees and their popularisation so that everyone takes ownership of this legal instrument and ensures its application towards eradicating the scourge of corruption.

a2273.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance and Economic Affairs Minister (budget winding-up speech)
a2273.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2273.title: Finance and Economic Affairs Minister (budget winding-up speech)
a2273.speech: Showed that government had listened to stakeholders' concerns about weak allocations to crucial sectors in the face of donor aid cuts by giving more to pro-poor and other neglected areas; according to Chithyola Banda, the top-up, estimated at a combined K52.2 billion, would help to improve implementation of government programmes and projects—ultimately enhancing service delivery in health, education and agriculture.

a2273.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance and Economic Affairs Minister
a2273.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2273.title: Finance and Economic Affairs Minister
a2273.speech: Said the additional funds to health will support HIV and Aids services, recruitment of frontline healthcare workers, operationalisation of the Malawi National Cancer Centre and new dialysis services at Mzuzu Central Hospital ; "We have ensured that all the affected critical services are provided for in the budget to ensure continued service delivery."

a2273.speaker: Mathews Ngwale, chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Health, and prominent health rights activists
a2273.name: Mathews Ngwale
a2273.title: chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Health, and prominent health rights activists
a2273.speech: Pleaded with government to increase funding to health to narrow the gap left by fleeing donors.

a2273.speaker: Senior Treasury official with intricate knowledge of the budget (anonymous source)
a2273.name: Senior Treasury official with intricate knowledge of the budget (anonymous source)
a2273.speech: Said the National Assembly's K11.7 billion addition is largely catering for members of Parliament's gratuities as they exit their term after the September 16 General Election, and that the top-up to the Legislature will also cater for new parliamentary constituencies following the redemarcation that saw the number jump by 36 from 193 in 2019 to 229 this year ; Said the fiscus did not factor in the proposed budget revenue from regularisation of kabaza operators, who are registering for tax compliance and other road fees payments that have already started flowing in, and added that government is also banking on ongoing fiscal consolidation within the public finance system to free up some resources and the aggressive implementation of the Domestic Resource Mobilisation Strategy.

a2273.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister, and Betchani Tchereni, Treasury Secretary (no response)
a2273.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2273.title: Finance Minister, and Betchani Tchereni, Treasury Secretary (no response)
a2273.speech: Were not immediately available to answer The Nation's question of where the additional money will come from for the top-up allocations.

a2308.speaker: Bank of Tanzania (BoT)
a2308.name: Bank of Tanzania (BoT)
a2308.speech: has warned of mounting economic pressures facing the region, urging stronger national responses to challenges such as the abrupt withdrawal of foreign aid and rising global tariffs.

a2308.speaker: Sauda Msemo, Bank of Tanzania Deputy Governor
a2308.name: Sauda Msemo
a2308.title: Bank of Tanzania Deputy Governor
a2308.speech: said countries must act swiftly to adjust to the changing financial landscape: "Various countries have different levels of reliance on foreign aid. Without it, many critical programmes and projects could be heavily impacted, threatening the hard-won recovery," she said ; "We have taken prompt measures, including reallocating the national budget to maintain progress."

a2308.speaker: Sauda Msemo, Bank of Tanzania Deputy Governor
a2308.name: Sauda Msemo
a2308.title: Bank of Tanzania Deputy Governor
a2308.speech: said that in Tanzania, the upcoming financial year beginning in July will include increased budgetary provisions aimed at cushioning the economy from further external shocks.

a2308.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Regional Economic Outlook report
a2308.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Regional Economic Outlook report
a2308.speech: showed that economic activity in sub-Saharan Africa exceeded expectations in 2024; the report indicates that the region’s GDP grew by 4.0 per cent last year, up from 3.6 per cent registered in 2023, and the IMF has slightly revised its forecasts, projecting growth to moderate to 3.8 per cent this year before rebounding to 4.2 per cent next year.

a2308.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.speech: noted that the slowdown in momentum has been driven largely by turbulent global conditions, citing subdued external demand, declining commodity prices, and tighter global financial conditions - particularly affecting commodity exporters and nations with stronger trade links to the US ; the outlook also highlighted that official development assistance to the region is expected to decline, adding further strain on vulnerable economies already grappling with funding shortfalls and rising borrowing costs.

a2308.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.speech: "After four years of crisis, authorities in sub-Saharan African countries already faced the complex challenge of maintaining economic stability while pursuing long-term development goals amid high social expectations," the IMF said.

a2308.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.speech: "Policymakers will need to increasingly draw on their own sources of strength," the IMF advised, stressing the importance of mobilising domestic revenue, improving spending efficiency, and strengthening fiscal frameworks.

a2308.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2308.speech: stressed that the private sector must play a greater role in driving sustainable development, and that structural reforms aimed at enhancing governance, improving the business climate, and deepening regional integration will be crucial.

a2375.speaker: U.S. Mission in Nigeria (statement)
a2375.name: U.S. Mission in Nigeria (statement)
a2375.speech: Issued a statement debunking claims that the visa reduction was retaliatory: "This reduction is not the result of any nation's stance on third-country deportees, the introduction of e-visa policies, or affiliations with groups like BRICS. The reduction in validity is part of an ongoing global review of the use of U.S. visas by other countries using technical and security benchmarks to safeguard U.S. immigration systems. We value our longstanding partnership with Nigeria and remain committed to working closely with the Nigerian public and government officials to help them meet those criteria and benchmarks, thereby ensuring safe, lawful, and mutually beneficial travel between our nations."

a2375.speaker: Bolaji Akinyemi, Nigeria's former Minister of Foreign Affairs and Chairman of the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA)
a2375.name: Bolaji Akinyemi
a2375.title: Nigeria's former Minister of Foreign Affairs and Chairman of the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA)
a2375.speech: In the 1980s, proposed the establishment of a Concert of Medium Powers - a group similar in concept to BRICS - intended to allow mid-sized nations to collectively influence global affairs and contribute to international stability and development ; also once advocated for Nigeria to develop nuclear capability - dubbed the "Black Bomb" - which could have made Nigeria the first Black nation with a nuclear weapon.

a2375.speaker: Opposition figures in the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC)
a2375.name: Opposition figures in the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC)
a2375.speech: Spun the recent mini-summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and five African heads of state in the White House on July 9 as a sign that the U.S. is shunning President Tinubu.

a2375.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a2375.name: Donald Trump
a2375.title: U.S. President
a2375.speech: During his recent meeting with African leaders, declared: "We're shifting from aid to trade. In the long run, this will be far more effective, sustainable, and beneficial than anything else that we could be doing together."

a2412.speaker: David Malpass, President of the World Bank
a2412.name: David Malpass
a2412.title: President of the World Bank
a2412.speech: Unexpectedly said he would resign in June on Wednesday.

a2412.speaker: World Bank 2021 annual report
a2412.name: World Bank 2021 annual report
a2412.speech: According to the bank's 2021 annual report, Malpass earned $525,000 in annual net salary that year, and the bank made more than $340,000 in annual contributions to a pension plan and other benefits.

a2412.speaker: U.S. officials, climate change experts and global development peers
a2412.name: U.S. officials
a2412.title: climate change experts and global development peers
a2412.speech: Floated names as possible candidates for the job, including Samantha Power (USAID Administrator), Rajiv Shah (Rockefeller Foundation president and former USAID administrator), Minouche Shafik and Wally Adeyemo.

a2412.speaker: Rockefeller Foundation
a2412.name: Rockefeller Foundation
a2412.speech: A philanthropic group that says it aims to "promote the well-being of humanity throughout the world."

a2465.speaker: King Mswati III of Eswatini
a2465.name: King Mswati III of Eswatini
a2465.speech: His Majesty King Mswati III's order that every local should be gainfully employed.

a2465.speaker: S'thofeni Ginindza, African Alliance
a2465.name: S'thofeni Ginindza
a2465.title: African Alliance
a2465.speech: His company plans to boost the hospitality and food sectors by building two new hotels to address the country's accommodation shortage. He stated that every after two years; his company would be constructing two hotels. Ginindza said they were tapping into beef production, since there was also a market for it, adding they would be exporting it to international markets. They also planned to expand their leading chicken business, Umbuluzi, reinforcing their position as the biggest chicken supplier in Eswatini.

a2465.speaker: Allen Kessler, African Food Security
a2465.name: Allen Kessler
a2465.title: African Food Security
a2465.speech: He said African Food Security was an American based company with ties all over Africa and their main focus was agriculture. He said they were working closely with the local communities, educating and involving them. He expressed gratitude in that the project had potential impact in Eswatini through job creation and new industry generation, which had the potential to play a pivotal role in the development of the country. He said they aspired to bring a programme driven by youth enhancement, sustainable farming practices and modern techniques integrated with skills transfer.

a2465.speaker: Ivan Sutherland, Royal Eswatini Sugar Corporation
a2465.name: Ivan Sutherland
a2465.title: Royal Eswatini Sugar Corporation
a2465.speech: His company's capital expenditure over the next five years is projected at E1.3 billion reoccurring and E2.5 billion new investments. He explained that they did not just deal with sugar and ethanol but also packing, ecotourism, wildlife and livestock. He said future plans under power generation were to generate between 50 and 80 Megawatts of power. He said they were looking for co-investment in the power generation project and implementation. He said the investment was between E6 and E10 billion and the project execution would start this year and expected to be completed by 2029. He also mentioned that they were producing rum and the capital cost was between E200 and E500 million. First brand would be launched by September. He said RES Corp was currently undertaking a high-level study on the feasibility of producing jet fuel and the capital cost was estimated to be between E2 and E4 billion. He said they were exploring a long-term possibility for investing in a plant valued between E3 and E5 billion for the manufacture of bio plastics, driven mainly by increasing environmental concerns, government regulations on plastic disposal as well as the demand for sustainable products. He said the global market was estimated to be about E20 billion.

a2465.speaker: Armandt Joubert, Voltalia Solar
a2465.name: Armandt Joubert
a2465.title: Voltalia Solar
a2465.speech: He said they were currently developing a 15 Megawatt solar PV project in the Lobombo region, estimated to be between E360 to E450 million. He explained that the typical project structure was 40 per cent local shareholding and Standard Bank was their lender and partner in the project. He said the estimated employment and local supply chain is 140 direct and indirect job opportunities during the construction phase. He said during the operations and maintenance, they estimated a minimum of 14 direct job opportunities for Emaswati. He said they were looking forward to supporting Eswatini in this investment and future investments to come.

a2465.speaker: Matt Sprague, Eswatini Metal Foundry
a2465.name: Matt Sprague
a2465.title: Eswatini Metal Foundry
a2465.speech: He said they also operated in three additional Southern African countries. Sprague said their purpose was to unlock value from scrap, create jobs and protect the environment. He said their vision was to drive industrial growth and self-reliance as well as reduce dependency on metal imports and increase local metal manufacturing. He said their key objective was to create a sustainable economy and generate employment and transfer skills and minimising landfill waste and improve waste management while enhancing national revenue and reducing metal and infrastructure theft and vandalism. He said once the licenses were granted, their plan was to implement phases one to four of the project and after six months they planned to have an operational aluminum and copper furnace. After 12 months they planned to have an operational battery recycling plan that would be recycling led batteries. He added that after 18 months, they planned to have an operational tyre and recycling plant which would be converting tyres and plastic into fuel. He said after 36 months, they also planned to have an operational steel furnace. He said the total capital investment for the projects was estimated at E625 million, including construction and infrastructure. He said their financial forecast was expected to start at E770 million annually and was expected to grow to about E1 billion annually. He said employment opportunities were projected to be about 500 direct and indirect jobs created and a skills transfer programme would be implemented. He said environmental benefits would include reducing outsourced fuel and reducing environmental impacts and reducing solid waste. He said tax compliance and reducing metal theft was another key component of the programme.

a2465.speaker: Wandile Hlatshwayo, Magomba Mining
a2465.name: Wandile Hlatshwayo
a2465.title: Magomba Mining
a2465.speech: Hlatshwayo said Magomba Mining began operations in January and they were now extracting coal. He said one of the pledges they were making was to become the platinum sponsor of the conference next year. He said Magomba Mining had employed over 500 Emaswati and expected to scale up to between 600 and 800 jobs created. He said in the next five to six months, they projected to extract 100 000 tones and in about two to three years they projected to be making a turnover of about E1.8 billion, equalling to about E1.2 billion after losses. He pledged that they would make a significant impact in the country's economic growth. He acknowledged the positive support from government.

a2465.speaker: Mike Flinn, Big Bend Textile Manufacturing Plant
a2465.name: Mike Flinn
a2465.title: Big Bend Textile Manufacturing Plant
a2465.speech: Flinn said they had secured E3.6 billion for a cotton value chain processing plant. Flinn highlighted that the project was part of the larger Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma water initiative, positioning cotton as the anchor crop. Flinn emphasised the importance of creating a self-sustaining ecosystem that benefits local farmers and manufacturers alike.

a2465.speaker: Tony Uzoebo, Kellogs Tolaram Eswatini Food Manufacturing
a2465.name: Tony Uzoebo
a2465.title: Kellogs Tolaram Eswatini Food Manufacturing
a2465.speech: According to Uzoebo, the Kellogs manufacturing plant currently generates E5 billion for Eswatini. He said by the end of 2025, they would be doubling the employment number of staff.

a2465.speaker: Nixon Dlamini, Eswatini Railways Matsapha Dry Port / Inland Container Depot (ICD) Expansion
a2465.name: Nixon Dlamini
a2465.title: Eswatini Railways Matsapha Dry Port / Inland Container Depot (ICD) Expansion
a2465.speech: According to Dlamini the expansion of this port will cost E149 million and will create employment for 212 people. Dlamini said this was one of the projects which are worth E300 million in total.

a2465.speaker: Dr Sam Sithole, Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise (EWADE)
a2465.name: Dr Sam Sithole
a2465.title: Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise (EWADE)
a2465.speech: Dr Sithole stated that their project was the Mkhondvo–Ngwavuma Water Augmentation Project (MNWAP) worth E32 billion. It is made out of four components, whereby one is the building of dams and one was already under construction, being Mpakeni Dam. The other component is agriculture, Dr Sithole said 30 00 hectares of land has been developed and will include the planting of cotton, industrial maize and Bana grass.

a2808.speaker: Scott Perry, U.S. Congressman
a2808.name: Scott Perry
a2808.title: U.S. Congressman
a2808.speech: on February 13, 2025, at the U.S. House subcommittee hearing titled 'War on Waste', alleged that USAID channel taxpayers' money amounting to approximately $697 million annually, sometimes in cash, to madrasas, and ultimately to radical groups. He specifically named ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram and ISIS Khorasan. Perry claimed the funds were diverted to training camps and terrorist operatives.

a2808.speaker: Ali Ndume, Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.name: Ali Ndume
a2808.title: Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.speech: raised the motion on the need to investigate USAID and other NGOs, and during the debate had said that a thorough investigation would end speculation about how non-state actors have managed to survive over the years. Asked how far his motion had gone: "Well, so far I have not heard anything about the motion. And I am handicapped, handicapped in the sense that what I did was what I am supposed to do, that is to raise the motion; and my prayer was for the Senate to investigate the matter. That motion was adopted, but up till now, I have not heard anything about that very important motion because I remember that the Senate resolved to invite the security chiefs. It is the work of the Senate leadership. You are right to ask me, but the best people to answer this is the leadership of the Senate."

a2808.speaker: Ali Ndume, Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.name: Ali Ndume
a2808.title: Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.speech: "Well, there will be light at the end of the tunnel depending on the commitment of the Nigerian government. Yes, this government has been investing, but it is not enough. I am still of the opinion that security and welfare of Nigerian citizens should be the top priority or the main priority of the government. And I also strongly believe that once our armed forces or security agencies are adequately funded and given the marching order, they can be achieved. Especially under the current leadership of the CDS (Chief of Defence Staff Christopher Musa) who leads the Air Force, the Army and the Navy. What they (the military) don't have is what I call TEAM: Training, Equipment, Ammunition, and Motivation." ; on the military's intelligence: "They have the right intelligence." ; on the CDS not being categorical about foreign funding: "No, that is because he is not to commit himself about that. But definitely, if the Nigerian armed forces are given what they need, I can assure you that they will deliver."

a2808.speaker: Ali Ndume, Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.name: Ali Ndume
a2808.title: Nigerian Senator (Borno South)
a2808.speech: On why it is difficult to come up with verifiable evidence of foreign funding: "No, it is not going down to that level. Give the armed forces what they need and they will get this thing done. In fact, now, especially in the North East, it boils down to three black spots - Mandara Mountains, Sambisa and the Lake Chad fringes. That is where they (Boko Haram) operate. If the Nigerian Armed Forces are given what they need, plus, for example, the support of Special Forces like the PMC (Private Military Contractors), they will succeed. They did it before. Boko Haram was chased out in collaboration with the Nigerian Armed Forces during President Jonathan's time. What stops us from doing that now? The American government, which is the strongest armed forces in the world, still uses private military contractors. France and Russia were using Wagner. I am an advocate of that, seriously, because this problem is hampering everything and it is spreading. It is like cancer. Once you don't get it done, whether by amputation or chemotherapy...it keeps spreading. The only safe place in Nigeria now, relatively, is the South West."

a2808.speaker: Ali Ndume, Nigerian Senator (then Chairman of Senate Committee on Army)
a2808.name: Ali Ndume
a2808.title: Nigerian Senator (then Chairman of Senate Committee on Army)
a2808.speech: In 2019, at a press briefing after returning from Borno, accused unnamed NGOs of connivance with Boko Haram: "Various NGOs in that area are conniving with the insurgents - providing them information, logistics and so many things."

a2808.speaker: Abdul Ningi, Nigerian Senator (PDP, Bauchi Central), co-sponsor of the motion
a2808.name: Abdul Ningi
a2808.title: Nigerian Senator (PDP, Bauchi Central), co-sponsor of the motion
a2808.speech: suggested that the security chiefs should first brief senators in a closed-door session.

a2808.speaker: Godswill Akpabio, Nigerian Senate President
a2808.name: Godswill Akpabio
a2808.title: Nigerian Senate President
a2808.speech: after ruling on the motion, had said, "If the closed-door briefing can substantiate that the USAID funds have indeed been misused to support terror activities, such allegations could strain Nigeria-US diplomatic relations. And if otherwise, the Senate might seek stronger international partnerships to counter-terrorism."

a2808.speaker: Yemi Adaramodu, Senator (APC, Ekiti South), chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, and Opeyemi Bamidele, Senate Leader (APC, Ekiti Central)
a2808.name: Yemi Adaramodu
a2808.title: Senator (APC, Ekiti South), chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, and Opeyemi Bamidele, Senate Leader (APC, Ekiti Central)
a2808.speech: neither answered phone calls nor responded to WhatsApp and text messages sent to them by our correspondent for details of their findings.

a2808.speaker: Policy and Legislative Advocacy Centre (PLAC) report, published March 19, 2025
a2808.name: Policy and Legislative Advocacy Centre (PLAC) report
a2808.title: published March 19, 2025
a2808.speech: "The Speaker of the House of Representatives has intervened in the action taken by the Ad hoc Committee investigating Nigerian Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and International Development partners over alleged links between USAID funding and the terrorist group Boko Haram, asking the Ad hoc Committee to stand down its probe. This decision comes after sustained concerns raised by NGOs regarding the committee's broad and intrusive demands, which they argue amount to an overreach and an infringement on their constitutional rights to operate... In the meeting, the Speaker acknowledged the overreach of the committee's actions and agreed that its demands extended beyond the scope of the investigation's intended purpose. He has consequently directed the Chairman of the Ad hoc Committee to stand down further action on the matter and explore a more collaborative and amicable means of engaging with NGOs, effectively ending the probe. The decision to suspend the investigation represents a significant victory for Nigeria's NGOs, reaffirming the need to uphold constitutional freedoms and protect NGOs from arbitrary government restrictions."

a2808.speaker: Musa Abdullahi Krishi, Special Adviser to the Speaker of the House of Representatives on Media and Publicity
a2808.name: Musa Abdullahi Krishi
a2808.title: Special Adviser to the Speaker of the House of Representatives on Media and Publicity
a2808.speech: "The Speaker's intervention on the matter was not to stall, suspend, stop, or end the Ad Hoc Committee's assignment, which was duly assigned/referred to it by the House at plenary after the adoption of a motion on the matter. From the reports available to the House leadership, there were insinuations that the Ad Hoc Committee tried to go beyond the constitutional boundaries of the powers of the National Assembly on investigating development partners and diplomatic missions. What the Speaker did was to call on the Committee to restrict its investigation to the constitutional powers of the parliament. Please, note that the Committee's assignment subsists, at the end of which it is expected to submit its report to the House for further action."

a2808.speaker: Malam Baba Isah, resident of Goneri village, Gujba Local Government Area, Yobe State
a2808.name: Malam Baba Isah
a2808.title: resident of Goneri village, Gujba Local Government Area, Yobe State
a2808.speech: "I am an eyewitness because we were held at the Boko Haram enclave at one time and we saw them cooking the same food items distributed to us in the town. They are the same bags and utensils. In fact, when Boko Haram annexed Buni Yadi town, they left behind many things that incriminated the NGOs. They left behind empty food bags and medicine sachets bearing the stickers of these organisations. Where did they get them from?"

a2808.speaker: Modu Garba, resident of Gamboru-Ngala town, Borno State
a2808.name: Modu Garba
a2808.title: resident of Gamboru-Ngala town, Borno State
a2808.speech: said he had been living in the area for 50 years but could not establish whether the insurgents were being sponsored by the USAID or other humanitarian aid partners: "All that we hear is that helicopters drop weapons and food for Boko Haram insurgents without solid evidence. We know they are getting weapons and food but no one can tell exactly where they get them from. I know that an NGO, Action Against Hunger, used to supply food to camps to feed repentant Boko Haram members but I cannot tell whether they also supply to the Boko Haram fighters in their enclaves. I don't know that."

a2808.speaker: Abba Baga, internally displaced person (IDP) from Baga
a2808.name: Abba Baga
a2808.title: internally displaced person (IDP) from Baga
a2808.speech: said many people around the Lake Chad region suspect USAID and other NGOs of "sponsoring" terrorists in the area: "For instance, the Boko Haram fighters live on the Tumbus (islands) and nobody goes there, but you will get intelligence from the NGOs that certain places should be avoided because of possible attack. We got such intelligence several times and the attacks happened. So, whether we like it or not, these organizations do spy on us and help the insurgents to fight us." ; called on the federal and state governments to take their engagements with the development partners with all sense of responsibility: "These people (terrorists) are comfortable there. They kidnapped someone and when he regained his freedom, he told me that they have everything there; they have a generating set to light up the place and eat food lavishly with assorted drinks. How are they getting all these?"

a2808.speaker: Colonel A. Ahmed (rtd), retired Nigerian Army officer who served in the North East
a2808.name: Colonel A. Ahmed (rtd)
a2808.title: retired Nigerian Army officer who served in the North East
a2808.speech: explained that the April 14, 2014, abduction of the Chibok girls brought about the international interest on Boko Haram and the rush by NGOs: "The rush by the NGOs coincided with the period Boko Haram was at its most dangerous, the era when global terrorism was at its peak with so many fronts in the limelight. These fuelled the belief that these NGOs were funding the terrorists in all aspects. These are mere allegations that are very strong and difficult to discard. Prior to 2014 when the NGOs were not in the conflict areas, there were no such allegations. I have operated in the conflict areas with the NGOs, arrested key Boko Haram members, interrogated and investigated several activities, yet there's no credible evidence as to the direct funding of Boko by the NGOs. All equipment used by the Boko Haram are either locally sourced or procured with the proceeds of crimes from the Sahel and Maghrib regions, which were well investigated and documented. But as long as USAID and the NGOs operate in the areas of conflict, as long as the allegations remain, Boko Haram will continue to benefit from the relief material directly and indirectly."

a2808.speaker: Colonel A. Ahmed (rtd), retired Nigerian Army officer who served in the North East
a2808.name: Colonel A. Ahmed (rtd)
a2808.title: retired Nigerian Army officer who served in the North East
a2808.speech: said the initial funding of Boko Haram under Mohammed Yusuf included contributions from members, farming activities by members, donations from well-to-do members and politicians, and trading and sales of religious materials; and that later funding when it became violent included contributions from members within Nigeria and from abroad, kidnapping, robbery, and protection taxes within their annexed territory, trading, drugs, and support from other terrorist organisations. He said USAID and other NGOs have a major responsibility of humanitarian assistance, especially in areas of health and education: "These organisations provided these supports to all assessed needy persons or communities within their areas of responsibilities. Boko Haram benefits through these supports mainly indirectly either through diversion or attacks on communities and IDP camps to steal the items provided by the NGOs. They tend to benefit more being that they have seeming freedom of action within the conflict areas."

a2808.speaker: Brigadier-General Sani Kukasheka Usman (rtd), former Director of Army Public Relations
a2808.name: Brigadier-General Sani Kukasheka Usman (rtd)
a2808.title: former Director of Army Public Relations
a2808.speech: "Allegations linking USAID and other NGOs to Boko Haram funding persist due to the complex nature of humanitarian work in insurgency-hit areas and the lack of clear, verifiable evidence. While public figures and the military have raised concerns, the challenge lies in the difficulty of tracing informal, cash-based terror financing and the allegations of suspected diversion of aid by NGOs to insurgents in the North East in particular. However, the absence of forensic financial trails and restricted access to some areas make it hard to establish a direct nexus. Rather than relying on suspicions, a more effective approach is to enhance transparency and accountability in aid operations. Many NGOs operate under genuine humanitarian mandates and their presence is often critical in regions the government cannot consistently reach, although many of them deviate from such policies and do things inimical to their mandate. A practical way forward is to deepen collaboration between aid agencies and security actors. The existing partnership between the Nigerian military and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), built on mutual respect and clearly defined boundaries, offers a model. Similar structured engagement, independent audits, and coordinated monitoring can help bridge the trust gap and ensure that humanitarian aid supports, rather than undermines national security."

a2808.speaker: Dr Kabiru Adamu, counterterrorism expert and Managing Director of Beacon Consulting
a2808.name: Dr Kabiru Adamu
a2808.title: counterterrorism expert and Managing Director of Beacon Consulting
a2808.speech: "Despite persistent denials from the now disbanded USAID and NGOs that it funded, allegations of their indirect involvement in funding terrorism, particularly by the nebulous group popularly called Boko Haram and other terrorist groups in Nigeria, continue to surface, fuelled by claims from U.S. and Nigerian lawmakers and the ensuing scrutiny by the Nigerian government. The recurring accusations, while largely unsubstantiated by concrete evidence linking legitimate aid to terror financing, highlight a deep-seated distrust and a complex landscape of suspicion surrounding international humanitarian efforts in conflict-ridden regions. USAID has vehemently refuted these claims, reaffirming its commitment to responsible assistance and condemning the violence perpetrated by Boko Haram. Similarly, many NGOs operating in Nigeria have pushed back against the probes, asserting that such investigations are 'unfair' and could hinder their crucial work in supporting vulnerable communities. There are indications that the Nigerian House of Representatives was made to stand down a broad investigation into NGOs, recognizing concerns about overreach and the potential to stifle legitimate civil society activities." ; said the persistence of these allegations can be attributed to several factors, including the opacities in terrorist financing: "The complex and often clandestine nature of these financial networks makes it challenging to definitively trace all funds and can lead to speculation about any large sums flowing into the region. Operating humanitarian programmes in conflict-affected areas like North East Nigeria presents immense logistical hurdles. Ensuring that aid reaches its intended beneficiaries without diversion or exploitation by armed groups is a constant struggle, even with stringent safeguards in place. This inherent difficulty can fuel public skepticism." ; "Allegations of this nature can also be influenced by political agendas, both domestic and international.
