They can serve to deflect blame, gain political leverage, or even undermine the credibility of foreign aid programmes."

a2808.speaker: Brigadier-General Tukur Gusau, Director of Defence Information, and Major-General Markus Kangye, Director of Defence Media Operations
a2808.name: Brigadier-General Tukur Gusau
a2808.title: Director of Defence Information, and Major-General Markus Kangye, Director of Defence Media Operations
a2808.speech: Several attempts made to get official comment from the Defence Headquarters proved abortive: Gusau referred our correspondent to Kangye, and when an inquiry was forwarded to Major-General Kangye on WhatsApp, it indicated that the message was read but it wasn't responded to as at when filing this report.

a2808.speaker: General Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a2808.name: General Christopher Musa
a2808.title: Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a2808.speech: has repeatedly highlighted the role of external support in sustaining terrorist activities in the country and reiterated his position; has consistently questioned how terrorist groups in Nigeria manage to sustain their operations despite sustained military offensives, pointing to foreign financial and logistical support as a critical factor; expressed concerns about the activities of international organisations operating in conflict zones, alleging that some of these entities indirectly support terrorist groups through funding and training, thereby prolonging the insurgency; cited instances where organisations ostensibly providing humanitarian aid paid up to ten years' rent in advance for properties in insurgency-prone areas, questioning whether these NGOs had foreknowledge that terrorism would persist for another decade. "As we speak, over 120,000 Boko Haram members have surrendered, and most of them came with hard currency. How did they get it? How are they funded? How did they get the training? How did they get the equipment?"

a2808.speaker: General Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a2808.name: General Christopher Musa
a2808.title: Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)
a2808.speech: during an interview with Aljazeera in January 2025, urged the United Nations to investigate the funding and training of Boko Haram terrorists: "The UN needs to come in because we need to trace the funding. It is an international flow, and we do not have control over that."

a2808.speaker: Source living in Washington (anonymous)
a2808.name: Source living in Washington (anonymous)
a2808.speech: "I live in the U.S and I can confidently tell you that the government simply views the opinion put out there by Congressman Perry as mere ranting of an opposition." ; said instead of addressing Perry's allegation separately, there was what he called "Broader oversight context" to the matter: "USAID's Office of Inspector General (OIG) has conducted investigations into past grants - such as the $110,000 award to Helping Hand for Relief & Development (HHRD), which had alleged terror links. However, these OIG probes did not address Perry's specific charges related to Boko Haram or ISIS."

a2808.speaker: U.S. Mission to Nigeria
a2808.name: U.S. Mission to Nigeria
a2808.speech: publicly stated that "comprehensive monitoring and evaluation systems are in place" to ensure aid reaches intended recipients and that they would investigate any proven misuse.

a2808.speaker: Ambassador Richard Mills, U.S. Ambassador to Nigeria
a2808.name: Ambassador Richard Mills
a2808.title: U.S. Ambassador to Nigeria
a2808.speech: said that there was "no evidence USAID funds Boko Haram," asserting that any credible findings would prompt immediate investigation in coordination with Nigerian authorities.

a2808.speaker: Zagazola Makama, counterinsurgency expert based in the North East
a2808.name: Zagazola Makama
a2808.title: counterinsurgency expert based in the North East
a2808.speech: said sources had confirmed to him the presence of foreign fighters linked to ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K) within ISWAP controlled territories: "In December 2024, at least nine foreign operatives, including two white men and seven light skinned individuals, were sighted in Monguno and Marte LGAs in Borno State. The fighters, believed to be from Pakistan and Afghanistan, were heavily armed and equipped with drones, cameras, recorders, and notepads, gathering information in ISWAP controlled areas. They spoke English and Arabic, with translations provided by an ISWAP interpreter fluent in Kanuri and Hausa. Three weeks later, on January 3, 2025, at approximately 1944Hrs, the group returned this time with ISWAP escort units mounted on motorcycles ferrying them between locations. During this visit, they were seen inquiring about ISWAP's taxation policies and its control over local farming, fishing, and market activities... A recent ISWAP video released by AMAQ confirmed that foreign ISIS fighters are actively training their West African counterparts in the Lake Chad region."

a2808.speaker: Top security operative (anonymous, 2019)
a2808.name: Top security operative (anonymous
a2808.speech: claimed that a captured Boko Haram commander confessed to receiving logistics support from NGOs: "The suspect confirmed that NGOs were supplying food and drugs to the terrorists in the forest."

a2808.speaker: Mohammed Tahir Monguno, then Representative, now Senate Chief Whip
a2808.name: Mohammed Tahir Monguno
a2808.title: then Representative, now Senate Chief Whip
a2808.speech: in a motion raised during plenary at the National Assembly in 2019, called for investigation into NGOs allegedly funding or aiding Boko Haram: "We should investigate activities of all NGOs operating in the country, in line with the possibility of their link to terrorist group Boko Haram..."

a2808.speaker: Hon. Gudaji Kazaure, former member of the House of Representatives
a2808.name: Hon. Gudaji Kazaure
a2808.title: former member of the House of Representatives
a2808.speech: made a remark during plenary on insecurity when he said: "The most important thing is for Mr President to be aware of those NGOs that are giving medication, support, food and others to the terrorists. If we don't stop those NGOs... we will not succeed in this war."

a2808.speaker: Governor Babagana Zulum of Borno State (official statement)
a2808.name: Governor Babagana Zulum of Borno State (official statement)
a2808.speech: called for an investigation after an NGO was found simulating weapons training in a hotel: "Pending the outcome of the police investigation, Governor Zulum has directed sealing of the hotel and suspension of ACTED from any humanitarian activity in the state," a statement said.

a2808.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a2808.name: Marco Rubio
a2808.title: U.S. Secretary of State
a2808.speech: On July 1, 2025, announced that USAID would cease independent foreign aid operations, transferring remaining aid responsibilities to the State Department.

a2839.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) and other public health entities
a2839.name: World Health Organization (WHO) and other public health entities
a2839.speech: have warned that the pandemic will be more lethal in Africa than in the developed regions thus far.

a2839.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the Horn of Africa countries
a2839.name: Heads of State and Government of the Horn of Africa countries
a2839.speech: decided at the end of March 2020 to adopt a joint strategy and to strengthen coordination and regional responses to curb the spread of the virus in the sub region; they announced their intention to coordinate regional response to the pandemic.

a2839.speaker: Heads of State and Government of the Horn of Africa countries (the leadership)
a2839.name: Heads of State and Government of the Horn of Africa countries (the leadership)
a2839.speech: recognized the central role and the need for proactive support of the African Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) through building the capacity of healthcare providers and emergency response teams, as well as provision of medical supplies including testing kits.

a2891.speaker: Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) (note)
a2891.name: Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) (note)
a2891.speech: According to ECHO's note, more than 4.4 million people are affected by flooding in these 6 countries, which has caused the destruction of houses, public health facilities, water systems, schools and sanitation facilities, as well as roads, infrastructure and farmland, plus a lack of access to drinking water, hygiene and sanitation services, increasing the risk of the spread of waterborne diseases ; Also according to ECHO, this funding will make it possible to provide immediate assistance and to meet the most urgent needs regarding food, shelter, access to drinking water, sanitation and other essential services in the hardest-hit areas, with the envelope distributed as follows: Chad: €1 million; Niger: €1,350,000; Nigeria: €1,100,000; Mali: €1,000,000 (656,000,000 FCFA); Cameroon: €650,000 and Burkina Faso: €300,000.

a2891.speaker: Janez Lenarcic, European Commissioner for Crisis Management
a2891.name: Janez Lenarcic
a2891.title: European Commissioner for Crisis Management
a2891.speech: Stated that excessive rainfall has struck the Sahel and Lake Chad regions with unprecedented impacts, displacing millions of people and causing considerable suffering and damage. “We are mobilising all the means at our disposal to come to the aid of the most vulnerable in the disaster-stricken countries, so that they can receive the assistance they so badly need,” he declared.

a2929.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.name: Elon Musk
a2929.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.speech: Denied leading a “hostile takeover” of the US government and defended his cost-cutting plans; described sweeping government cuts as “common sense” measures that are “not draconian or radical” ; “The people voted for major government reform and that’s what the people are going to get. That’s what democracy is all about.” ; “It’s not optional for us to reduce the federal expenses. It’s essential. It’s essential for America to remain solvent as a country.”

a2929.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.name: Elon Musk
a2929.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.speech: “I fully expect to be scrutinised. It’s not like I think I can get away with something.” ; said the public could take its own view about potential conflicts of interest.

a2929.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.name: Elon Musk
a2929.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.speech: Described federal workers as an “unelected, fourth, unconstitutional branch of government” that he said has “more power than any elected representative”.

a2929.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.name: Elon Musk
a2929.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a2929.speech: Asked about a recent false claim that the US government was sending millions of dollars worth of condoms to Gaza: “Some of the things that I say will be incorrect and should be corrected.”

a2929.speaker: US President Donald Trump
a2929.name: US President Donald Trump
a2929.speech: “We found fraud and abuse,” Trump said of Musk’s work on Tuesday, without providing evidence. He estimated more than $1 trillion in wasteful spending would be discovered although gave no further details.

a2929.speaker: US President Donald Trump
a2929.name: US President Donald Trump
a2929.speech: “I hope that the court system is going to allow us to do what we have to do,” referring to recent judgments that have temporarily halted his efforts to shrink government, including through an employee buyout programme.

a2929.speaker: US President Donald Trump
a2929.name: US President Donald Trump
a2929.speech: Said that if the White House thought there was a lack of transparency or a conflict of interest, “we would not let him do that segment or look in that area”.

a2929.speaker: Democrats
a2929.name: Democrats
a2929.speech: Have criticised the agency and accused it of a lack of transparency, and have accused Musk of personally benefiting from some of the changes the Trump administration is trying to push through.

a2929.speaker: Chuck Schumer, Senate Minority Leader
a2929.name: Chuck Schumer
a2929.title: Senate Minority Leader
a2929.speech: “An unelected shadow government is conducting a hostile takeover of the federal government.” He said Democrats would work to block Musk’s efforts by introducing specific language into spending bills.

a2929.speaker: Executive order signed by Trump
a2929.name: Executive order signed by Trump
a2929.speech: Instructed Doge to “significantly” cut down the size of the federal workforce; the order also calls on government offices to “undertake plans for large-scale reductions in force”, and says that once a hiring freeze that Trump signed on his first day ends, agencies should hire no more than one person for every four who depart.

a2929.speaker: CBS News poll (BBC’s US partner)
a2929.name: CBS News poll (BBC’s US partner)
a2929.speech: Indicated a majority of Americans are in favour of Musk’s work, but disagree over how much influence he should have; it suggested Republicans in particular supported his efforts to cut federal spending and foreign aid; the poll indicated largely favourable ratings for Trump’s policies, however, some 66% of people said they wanted him to focus more on lowering prices.

a2929.speaker: USAID inspector general (report)
a2929.name: USAID inspector general (report)
a2929.speech: Released a report criticising plans to put the vast majority of the agency’s staff on leave and close US-backed aid programmes around the world; the inspector general was fired one day later.

a2979.speaker: Steward Nankhumwa, 25-year-old college student based in Zomba
a2979.name: Steward Nankhumwa
a2979.title: 25-year-old college student based in Zomba
a2979.speech: “In the past, storm and cyclone-induced floods were not occurring at the rate they are doing now. Not nowadays. We hear about storms and cyclones causing devastation in Malawi almost every year, which signals a problem” ; Says he has had nightmares about floods, such that he decided to do something about the situation, devising a solution, namely the introduction of a floods alarm in Likangala River.

a2979.speaker: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment Report (on Cyclone Freddy)
a2979.name: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment Report (on Cyclone Freddy)
a2979.speech: Estimating that 225 people died, 109,625 hectares of crops for around 308,000 farming families getting washed away, with over 288,000 houses damaged and total damage and losses estimated at $220.2 million.

a2979.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma)
a2979.name: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma)
a2979.speech: Indicated that Cyclone Chido, in December 2024, affected 46,017 people in 23 districts, with 13 people dying, 29 sustaining injuries and members of 227 households getting displaced ; Indicated that the rains induced by Cyclone Jude affected 3,600 people in the Southern Region, with three people reported missing; later, it said bodies of two of the missing people had been found ; Also indicates that apart from 774 people that are reported to have been affected in TA Nkanda, the council received reports of damage from TA Njema and Sunganinzeru.

a2979.speaker: Robert Nayeja, Nsanje District Council spokesperson
a2979.name: Robert Nayeja
a2979.title: Nsanje District Council spokesperson
a2979.speech: Said searches led to the recovery of the bodies of Joe Tisowa, 26, and 11-year-old Chifundo Patrick.

a2979.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
a2979.name: Charles Kalemba
a2979.title: Dodma Commissioner
a2979.speech: Said thirteen Southern Region districts were affected by the cyclone, and indicated that the three people went missing after a canoe they were sailing in capsized in Ruo River.

a2979.speaker: Chikwawa District Council (report)
a2979.name: Chikwawa District Council (report)
a2979.speech: A Chikwawa District Council report indicates that three houses collapsed in TA Mulilima’s area.

a2979.speaker: Zomba City Council (report)
a2979.name: Zomba City Council (report)
a2979.speech: A Zomba City report indicates that 19 households (approximately 86 people) have been affected.

a2979.speaker: Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (Met)
a2979.name: Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (Met)
a2979.speech: Has indicated that the cyclone made landfall in Malawi through Phalombe District.

a2979.speaker: Dr Lucy Mtilatila, director of the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services
a2979.name: Dr Lucy Mtilatila
a2979.title: director of the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services
a2979.speech: “The storm reduced its intensity when it was approaching Malawi”

a2979.speaker: Burnet Khulumbo, Care Malawi Humanitarian Assistance Programme Manager
a2979.name: Burnet Khulumbo
a2979.title: Care Malawi Humanitarian Assistance Programme Manager
a2979.speech: Indicates that they want to ease the suffering of people who have been affected by natural phenomena ; “Care Malawi [also] issued cash to people who were affected by drought, which affected crops in Mangochi and some parts of the country during the last farming seasons” ; “The money will be paid for three months, starting from this month [March].”

a2979.speaker: World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), ‘State of the Global Climate’ report issued in Geneva on March 19, 2025
a2979.name: World Meteorological Organisation (WMO)
a2979.title: ‘State of the Global Climate’ report issued in Geneva on March 19, 2025
a2979.speech: Key climate indicators reached record levels last year, with long-term warming remaining below 1.5 degrees Celsius, sea-level rise and ocean warming remaining “irreversible” for hundreds of years; it also indicates that “record” greenhouse gas concentrations combined with El Niño and other factors driving record heat during the year in question; the report further shows that “globally, each of the past 10 years were individually the warmest. Atmospheric concentrations of carbon dioxide are at the highest levels in the last 800,000 years”; it cites early warnings and the provision of timely climate services as key to “protecting communities and economies”.

a2979.speaker: António Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General
a2979.name: António Guterres
a2979.title: United Nations Secretary-General
a2979.speech: “Our planet is issuing more distress signals—but this report shows that limiting long-term global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius is still possible. Leaders must step up to make it happen—seizing the benefits of cheap, clean renewables for their people and economies— with new national climate plans due this year.”

a2979.speaker: Celeste Saulo, WMO Secretary-General
a2979.name: Celeste Saulo
a2979.title: WMO Secretary-General
a2979.speech: “While a single year above 1.5 °C of warming does not indicate that the long-term temperature goals of the Paris Agreement are out of reach, it is a wake-up call that we are increasing the risks to our lives, economies and to the planet.”

a2979.speaker: Fedson Chikuse, Dodma Deputy Director responsible for preparedness
a2979.name: Fedson Chikuse
a2979.title: Dodma Deputy Director responsible for preparedness
a2979.speech: Pointed out, speaking at the meeting that was held in November last year, that before Cyclone Freddy and last year’s El-Nino spate, Malawians lacked anticipatory actions, hence natural phenomena’s impacts were devastating on communities ; “Anticipatory action offers a powerful pathway to mitigate these impacts. By acting early, lives can be protected, livelihoods safeguarded and emergency response costs reduced.”

a2979.speaker: Chifundo Kalulu, secretary general of the Malawi Red Cross Society
a2979.name: Chifundo Kalulu
a2979.title: secretary general of the Malawi Red Cross Society
a2979.speech: Acknowledges that prioritising anticipatory action and disaster preparedness can help Malawi minimise the devastating impacts of disasters and promote resilience among community members; he says putting in place such a mechanism “is not merely a matter of policy; it is a matter of survival, particularly in the face of escalating climate risks and other challenges” that are affecting Malawi and other countries.

a2979.speaker: Edwin Zawanda, Dodma Principal Disaster Preparedness Officer
a2979.name: Edwin Zawanda
a2979.title: Dodma Principal Disaster Preparedness Officer
a2979.speech: In February this year singled out anticipatory humanitarian action as a viable long-term strategy for mitigating the impacts of perennial floods, including problems such as loss of lives and property; adds that apart from taking anticipatory action, there are other mechanisms employed to ensure that people remain safe from disasters, natural or otherwise ; “In fact, in Nsanje and Chikwawa, we moved people from disaster-prone areas to upper areas. Not only that, we are taking steps to sensitise community members, in terms of disaster preparedness. In addition to such actions, the new Disaster Risk Management Act empowers Dodma to make sure that people move from disaster-prone areas to areas where they will be safe. As for those who are sticking to such areas, there are regulations that ensure that they move from such areas.”

a2979.speaker: Trywell Khonje, Eagles Relief Programmes Officer
a2979.name: Trywell Khonje
a2979.title: Eagles Relief Programmes Officer
a2979.speech: Has described anticipatory action as a significant short to medium-term strategic plan of minimising the impact of floods in vulnerable areas; he explains that the framework, which is a new concept in Malawi, will enable community members to develop tailored disaster-preparedness interventions ; “Local community members will, among other things, facilitate the process of identifying potential actions to implement between the time an early warning message is received and the onset of a disaster in communities. What happens is that between the time an early warning has been issued and time of disaster, the period in-between is ideal for anticipatory action. We have anticipatory action at district level, contained in the district contingency plan. Common anticipatory actions include cash transfers to households; strengthening of structures, including providing black plastic material; and, in extreme situations, promoting the early harvesting of crops” ; “However, in cases of floods, you are very limited, in terms of anticipatory actions, because you have very few days during which to take action. It must be noted that [anticipatory action] is implemented if we have 85 percent probability of disaster.”

a3331.speaker: A group of non-government organisations (NGOs) working in Sudan
a3331.name: A group of non-government organisations (NGOs) working in Sudan
a3331.speech: Said about 2.8 million people in and around El Fasher in North Darfur currently have no option to escape or to access much needed assistance; about 500,000 people are living in Zamzam refugee camp near El Fasher which is experiencing famine.

a3331.speaker: Aid workers from international NGOs working in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Aid workers from international NGOs working in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: Said children were witnessing atrocities no child should see which was impacting their behaviour with many becoming anxious, not sleeping and suffering psychological distress; some boys were joining fighters and some girls marrying fighters as a means of survival to get food; others were eating leaves to survive.

a3331.speaker: Jamal*, 45, operations staff at an international NGO in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Jamal*
a3331.title: 45, operations staff at an international NGO in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "The scale of human suffering that we are seeing is hard to put into words, and it's only getting worse. On a daily basis, I see bodies on the road and children fleeing their home without their parents or any belongings. There are soldiers fighting in front of our homes and in the market, and there are bombs and airstrikes, the shooting is everywhere. Violence against women is terrible. Women have been kidnapped and raped when going into the market. Community members tell us that young girls have been forced to marry fighters, and young women are engaging in survival sex in exchange for food, water, and cash. People around me don't have food. They are eating leaves from trees. Many young people are joining the fighters to access food. We take advantage of the three to four hours when there is no shooting or shelling to do some critical activities like water trucking in the gathering point to ensure that displaced people have access to clean water. We are worried millions of people will die unless the world pays attention and listens to us."

a3331.speaker: Mohamad*, 52, administration staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Mohamad*
a3331.title: 52, administration staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "In May, four of my neighbours were killed inside their homes. Many homes were destroyed and burnt, and the properties of residents looted. Many people fled to safer places outside of El Fasher, but now are living in miserable conditions without receiving any humanitarian assistance. There is no possibility to leave home due to roadblocks, either due to the rains and floods, or because of the armed groups. The tight siege has had a terrible impact on our lives. Children have been forced to beg to survive - they do not have enough food. My family has moved to different locations and in different directions, our communications have been cut off and I'm uncertain when to meet them again."

a3331.speaker: Omar*, 42, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Omar*
a3331.title: 42, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "The children I work with tell me that they have lost their mother, their father, their homes. They say they go to sleep without food, and sometimes only have one meal per day. I see children crying... and I've noticed changes in their behaviour - poor sleep, more anxiety, a lack of appetite, depression, and psychological distress. The situation around me is difficult, there is a lot of shelling, bombing, and ammunition everywhere. We aren't able to move to the market or go to the mosque. Feeling safe has become a dream."

a3331.speaker: Abdul*, 36, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Abdul*
a3331.title: 36, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "In September 2024, there was an attack on my uncle's house. My cousin and the neighbour's son died in the family home from the shelling, and my uncle's wife was badly injured and is still in the hospital. On the same day, we lost five of my family members. I am living in El Fasher with my parents and my wife and three children. I can't leave El Fasher because my mother and father are old and cannot bear the long distance and the fatigue of travelling. But now the situation is so difficult, we are only eating two meals a day."

a3331.speaker: Majeed*, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Majeed*
a3331.title: child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "I heard just recently five people lost their lives in the market from an attack, and two children lost their legs. I'm seeing the behaviour change with the children that I work with. They are sleeping poorly, they are anxious, they aren't eating well. They tell me they are scared of the war and want to be somewhere safe. They want the war to end."

a3331.speaker: Rifat*, 54, water and sanitation staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Rifat*
a3331.title: 54, water and sanitation staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "I saw with my own eyes two children die immediately and more than five injured while they were in a gathering place in town. Children are telling us to stop this conflict, that they don't want more children to die. I've seen other children also keeping silent and going quiet, and becoming isolated from others."

a3331.speaker: Wajih*, 55, education and child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Wajih*
a3331.title: 55, education and child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "Just two days ago I was on the way to Zamzam camp and in front of our vehicle there was an artillery bombing, with six street children killed. It was shocking. The children I work with say they are suffering, some children are telling us horrible things they have seen which have affected their ability to sleep. We are supporting these children how we can but it isn't enough."

a3331.speaker: Amar*, 43, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.name: Amar*
a3331.title: 43, child protection staff with an international organisation in El Fasher (anonymous)
a3331.speech: "A month and a half ago there was an incident near my home where four children were killed and 14 others injured when they were shelled while playing football in an open space. And three months ago, there was shelling that hit close to where I live, killing three adults and three children inside their home. Children keep asking me when the war will be over. They are anxious."

a3331.speaker: Joint statement of CARE International, Danish Refugee Council, GOAL Global, Norwegian Refugee Council, Plan International, Relief International, Save the Children International and Solidarites International
a3331.name: Joint statement of CARE International
a3331.title: Danish Refugee Council, GOAL Global, Norwegian Refugee Council, Plan International, Relief International, Save the Children International and Solidarites International
a3331.speech: Calling for the following immediate actions: parties to conflict must protect civilian areas such as displacement shelters, including Zamzam camp, and immediately halt military operations around El Fasher and Zamzam camp that put civilians at risk; parties to conflict must uphold international humanitarian law, including the protection of civilians, and end indiscriminate targeting of civilians, refrain from using starvation or sexual violence as a weapon of war, and prevent mass atrocities; parties to conflict must protect humanitarian workers and assets and remove all obstacles to the sustained, timely, effective and principled delivery of humanitarian assistance, including through both cross-border and cross-line entry points, and open safe passage for food, medical aid, and medical, humanitarian and commercial supplies, particularly in Zamzam; all stakeholders must increase diplomatic pressure on conflict parties and their backers to facilitate the critical work of humanitarian organisations and increase public condemnation of denials of humanitarian access; all parties must explicitly condemn the increasing cases of gender based violence, including sexual violence; and parties to conflict and those with influence must work together to reach an immediate and lasting country-wide ceasefire. The statement also says El Fasher has become hell on earth for thousands of women, children and other vulnerable people.

a3411.speaker: Izbath Djaboutouboutou, Director of the Self-Referral Unit of the Ombudsman of the Republic of Benin and focal point for the project
a3411.name: Izbath Djaboutouboutou
a3411.title: Director of the Self-Referral Unit of the Ombudsman of the Republic of Benin and focal point for the project
a3411.speech: Said that young people's civic engagement and leadership are valuable resources only if they are cultivated and supported; notes that thanks to the various teams deployed in the seven communes of the northern departments, 1,282 young women and men have been trained and are now equipped to contribute actively to the development of their communities and, by extension, to the development of the country, and are better prepared to take part in nation-building with an emphasis on peace and national unity.

a3411.speaker: Abigail Slenski, USAID Deputy Country Representative in Benin
a3411.name: Abigail Slenski
a3411.title: USAID Deputy Country Representative in Benin
a3411.speech: Observes that by coming together to prepare their advocacy points and discuss their perspectives with the Technical and Financial Partners, these young people are demonstrating their determination to make their voices and aspirations heard in order to strengthen peace and social cohesion in their communities; remains convinced that the discussions during the workshop will be rich and fruitful, leading to the formulation of relevant and impactful advocacy points: "However, we remain very active in ensuring a smooth transition of support to young people in the North," she promised, inviting participants to take full advantage of the workshop by establishing solid connections and lasting commitments with the other programmes and partners present.

a3466.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a3466.name: Elon Musk
a3466.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a3466.speech: Announced that the US Agency for International Development (USAID) should “die”; called USAID a “criminal organisation” after security officials reportedly denied members of his cost-cutting team access to secure areas at the agency's headquarters in Washington, DC ; “It's time for it to die,” he wrote on his social media platform X.

a3466.speaker: Al Jazeera (news report)
a3466.name: Al Jazeera (news report)
a3466.speech: According to Al Jazeera, Musk, appointed by US President Donald Trump to lead the department, called USAID a “criminal organisation” after security officials reportedly refused members of his cost-cutting team access to classified areas at the agency's headquarters in Washington, DC.

a3466.speaker: Several US media outlets (reports)
a3466.name: Several US media outlets (reports)
a3466.speech: Reported that USAID's Director of Security, John Voorhees, and his deputy, Brian McGill, were placed on leave after refusing to allow DOGE officials into secure areas because they did not have security clearance.

a3466.speaker: CNN and other reports
a3466.name: CNN and other reports
a3466.speech: According to several reports, including one first reported by CNN, DOGE members — acting under a Trump executive order but not as an official government department — were able to gain access to areas containing classified information after the standoff.

a3466.speaker: Steven Cheung, White House Director of Communications
a3466.name: Steven Cheung
a3466.title: White House Director of Communications
a3466.speech: Denied that DOGE officials had tried to enter highly secure areas, calling a PBS report about the incident “fake news” and “not true at all” ; “This is what careless and unreliable media look like,” Cheung wrote on X.

a3466.speaker: Katie Miller, DOGE staff member
a3466.name: Katie Miller
a3466.title: DOGE staff member
a3466.speech: Appeared to confirm the task force's attempt to enter, writing on X that “no classified materials were accessed without proper security clearances.”

a3466.speaker: Chris Coons, Democratic Senator from Delaware
a3466.name: Chris Coons
a3466.title: Democratic Senator from Delaware
a3466.speech: “President Trump has spent two weeks harassing and dismissing USAID employees, and now his team is trying to destroy the agency completely,” he wrote on his X page.

a3466.speaker: Jeremy Konyndyk, former Director of USAID's Office of Foreign Disaster Assistance (2013-2017)
a3466.name: Jeremy Konyndyk
a3466.title: former Director of USAID's Office of Foreign Disaster Assistance (2013-2017)
a3466.speech: Said abolishing USAID without the approval of the US Congress is illegal and a violation of the separation of powers protected by the US Constitution ; “If this attempt succeeds and if Trump (or Elon) can ignore the laws of Congress and funding directives, and Congress stays silent, then this is a very bad sign and it will not stop at USAID alone,” Konyndyk wrote on X.

a3466.speaker: Democratic members of Congress
a3466.name: Democratic members of Congress
a3466.speech: Have also expressed their concern about Musk's great influence in the government despite his not holding an elected office.

a3466.speaker: The New York Times and the Associated Press (reports)
a3466.name: The New York Times and the Associated Press (reports)
a3466.speech: Reported at the weekend that DOGE had gained access to the federal government's payment system, which holds sensitive personal information on millions of Americans.

a3466.speaker: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, US Representative from New York
a3466.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
a3466.title: US Representative from New York
a3466.speech: “This is a massive danger,” she wrote on X. “People elected Donald Trump as President, not Elon Musk. Having an unelected billionaire, indebted and with private foreign interests, stealing classified US information is a major threat to national security. This should not be a partisan issue.”

a3466.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3466.name: Donald Trump
a3466.title: US President
a3466.speech: On Sunday told reporters that his administration would remove “left-wing lunacy” from USAID before making a decision about its future.

a3466.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3466.name: Donald Trump
a3466.title: US President
a3466.speech: Later emphasised aid to South Africa, pledging to halt all future funding to that country over land expropriation and, according to him, the harming of other people ; “The United States will not accept this, we will take action,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, adding that the funding freeze would last until a full investigation of the situation is completed.

a3466.speaker: US government data
a3466.name: US government data
a3466.speech: According to US government figures, the United States allocated about $440 million in aid to South Africa in 2023; Washington provided a total of $72 billion in foreign aid to about 180 countries in 2023, with more than half of that money disbursed through USAID.

a3714.speaker: Luís Mado, EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.name: Luís Mado
a3714.title: EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.speech: Interviewed by AIM, said the amount of over 700 million US dollars in the project portfolio is also aimed at investing in power generation plants across the country ; revealed that, at the same time, the company is investing 50 million dollars annually to retain existing customers and ensure grid stability: “We have several transmission and distribution projects underway that will strengthen the grid and ensure connectivity with neighboring countries. The line to Malawi is one of the milestones we hope to complete by the end of the year.”

a3714.speaker: Luís Mado, EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.name: Luís Mado
a3714.title: EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.speech: Explained that in the generation sector, EDM is investing in key power plants, such as the Temane Power Plant in the southern province of Inhambane, with a capacity of 450 megawatts (MW), which has already entered the final construction phase: “The Temane Power Plant experienced some delays due to Cyclone Idai, but it has now resumed. The associated transmission line is complete, and the plant should begin injecting power into the grid soon.”

a3714.speaker: Luís Mado, EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.name: Luís Mado
a3714.title: EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.speech: Said another strategic project is the Mphanda Nkuwa hydro-electric project, on the Zambezi river, in the central province of Tete, which is expected to add 1,500 MW to the national energy matrix “and will be essential for meeting growing industrial and export demand” ; warned: “We must fight to ensure that projects like Mphanda Nkuwa become a reality in the next five to six years. Otherwise, the country could face an energy deficit.”

a3714.speaker: Luís Mado, EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.name: Luís Mado
a3714.title: EDM Director of Transmission
a3714.speech: Revealed that EDM faces difficulties in anticipating the installation of new industries, which often arrive before the electricity grid: “Industry is installed first, and only then do we bring energy. This has to change. We need to ensure that when companies arrive, they already have electricity available.”

a3836.speaker: Gregory T. Blamoh, Secretary General of the Liberia National Red Cross Society (LNRCS)
a3836.name: Gregory T. Blamoh
a3836.title: Secretary General of the Liberia National Red Cross Society (LNRCS)
a3836.speech: Emphasized the importance of community involvement in the recovery process: "Together, we are helping communities recover and build back stronger. The Red Cross and its partners are not only providing immediate relief but also working closely with the affected families to promote long-term resilience. Community engagement in activities like drainage clearing is critical to reducing the impact of future floods." ; Reiterated the organization's commitment to supporting flood-affected communities in their efforts to recover, rebuild, and enhance their resilience in the face of growing climate-related challenges.

a3974.speaker: President of the APAM Association (Association Pour un Avenir Meilleur d’Ali-Sabieh)
a3974.name: President of the APAM Association (Association Pour un Avenir Meilleur d’Ali-Sabieh)
a3974.speech: Opened the ceremony with a speech detailing the different phases of the project and the technical support provided by the regional hospital during the awareness-raising phase on good hygiene practice in the storage of drinking water; stressed the importance of community engagement and collaboration with local institutions to guarantee the success and sustainability of such initiatives.

a3974.speaker: Aden Abdillahi Ali, Secretary General of the Regional Council
a3974.name: Aden Abdillahi Ali
a3974.title: Secretary General of the Regional Council
a3974.speech: Recalled the significant role of civil society associations in contributing to the socio-economic development of their region while improving the living conditions of the local population, with the support of the regional authorities and development partners.

a3974.speaker: Mahdi Adaweh Bouh, representative of the Prefecture
a3974.name: Mahdi Adaweh Bouh
a3974.title: representative of the Prefecture
a3974.speech: Praised the efforts of the members of the APAM association for providing two 300-litre tanks to some sixty families, a handover that comes at an opportune moment, in the middle of the hot season; also praised the collaboration with the regional hospital, whose health care professionals participated extensively in raising awareness of good hygiene practices.

a4212.speaker: Kingdom Mamba, Office of the Labour Commissioner (Eswatini)
a4212.name: Kingdom Mamba
a4212.title: Office of the Labour Commissioner (Eswatini)
a4212.speech: Confirmed that the mine has halted operations, leading to the retrenchment of about 86 employees: “We are aware of the matter. The company has notified us about its retrenchment, where 86 employees have been affected due to volatile prices in the markets as a result of Rand fluctuations in the South African markets. The 86 have been paid their terminal benefits.”

a4212.speaker: One of the affected Mhlume mine employees (anonymous)
a4212.name: One of the affected Mhlume mine employees (anonymous)
a4212.speech: Said he was deeply worried as he was unsure whether operations would resume any time soon.

a4212.speaker: Other affected Mhlume mine employees (anonymous)
a4212.name: Other affected Mhlume mine employees (anonymous)
a4212.speech: Confirmed that they had been officially informed by management that, due to a lack of business, operations had been halted.

a4212.speaker: One of the Mhlume mine workers (anonymous)
a4212.name: One of the Mhlume mine workers (anonymous)
a4212.speech: Added that signs of trouble had appeared about three months ago, when business began to slow down: “What we have been told is that there is no market for now. We will just live in hope that soon, things will normalise, and we will be given another chance.”

a4212.speaker: Peter Grey, Managing Director of the mine (non-response)
a4212.name: Peter Grey
a4212.title: Managing Director of the mine (non-response)
a4212.speech: Messages sent to the mine’s Managing Director, Peter Grey, had not been responded to; efforts to obtain a comment from management were unsuccessful at the time of compiling this report.

a4212.speaker: Nozwelakhe Mamba, Project Coordinator of the mine (non-response)
a4212.name: Nozwelakhe Mamba
a4212.title: Project Coordinator of the mine (non-response)
a4212.speech: Requested a questionnaire but had also not reverted.

a4212.speaker: Maloma Colliery Limited (announcement)
a4212.name: Maloma Colliery Limited (announcement)
a4212.speech: Announced last month that it had been forced to reduce production and retrench 145 more employees after its biggest customer scaled down operations.

a4212.speaker: Times of Eswatini (sister publication report)
a4212.name: Times of Eswatini (sister publication report)
a4212.speech: As reported by our sister publication, the Times of Eswatini, Maloma Colliery Limited’s clients are smelters who use anthracite coal primarily for two purposes: providing heat and acting as a reducing agent.

a4212.speaker: Japie Fullard, Glencore Ferroalloys Chief Executive Officer (communiqué)
a4212.name: Japie Fullard
a4212.title: Glencore Ferroalloys Chief Executive Officer (communiqué)
a4212.speech: Informed employees that retrenchments were imminent at Boshoek, Wonderkop Smelters, Rhovan Operations, and the Carbon Division: “As part of this process, we are also contemplating reducing the Lion Smelter to a two-furnace operation and will proceed with further streamlining and restructuring the support functions within the Mining Division, at Rustenburg and Lydenburg Smelters, Head Office and Shared Services functions. Rhovan will continue operating with a new product mix and potentially a different structure.” ; added that consultations would be held with affected employees and their representatives to explore all possible options to mitigate the impact on the workforce, including alternatives to retrenchment.

a4212.speaker: South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC)
a4212.name: South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC)
a4212.speech: According to the SABC, the closure of these mines has resulted in job losses exceeding 3 500, affecting thousands of families.

a4212.speaker: Dr Noah Nhleko, Commissioner of Mines (Eswatini)
a4212.name: Dr Noah Nhleko
a4212.title: Commissioner of Mines (Eswatini)
a4212.speech: Expressed hope that the challenging situation currently facing Eswatini’s coal mining sector will improve; confirmed that the management of the affected mine had informed him of the difficulties they are experiencing, noted that the mine’s management had handled the matter appropriately, including maintaining communication with his office, and explained that the main issue lies in the South African market, which has been affected by rising electricity costs and the introduction of an export tax: “They have been working hard to establish the plant. As far as I know, they have followed all the necessary procedures, including notifying the labour commissioner.” ; “As government, we are hopeful that the markets will improve because we become very concerned when emaSwati lose jobs. We do understand that there are global challenges, and we sympathise with the mining companies.”

a4337.speaker: Council of Ministers of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4337.name: Council of Ministers of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4337.speech: Said the PESOE 2026 "guides the careful and strategic allocation of public resources, ensuring compliance with the targets of the Government's Five-Year Programme" ; said the allocation of resources for 2026 "focuses on investment in productive, logistical and social infrastructure, with emphasis on transport, digitalisation, roads, education and health."

a4337.speaker: Council of Ministers of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4337.name: Council of Ministers of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4337.speech: Wrote of the Legislative Authorisation draft law that "the Law will allow the approval of a normative framework covering the organisation of commercial activity and the provision of mercantile services, notably provisions on the classification of the commercial network and of the provision of mercantile services according to their size; the different activities carried out by traders and the sales modalities of the different activities carried out by traders; the framework of guarantees for goods and after-sales services; and the definition of the forms of territorial establishment of commercial premises in urban, suburban and rural areas."

a4373.speaker: JoEllen Gorg, Acting U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4373.name: JoEllen Gorg
a4373.title: Acting U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4373.speech: In her remarks underscored the core values underpinning the American ethos: “Every Fourth of July, across the United States, millions of Americans reflect on values that have defined us for nearly 250 years: freedom, excellence, and opportunity.” ; “These ideals not only fuel our national spirit but underpin our international relations. Today, as we celebrate American independence, we also celebrate our enduring partnership with Nigeria. A partnership rooted in expanded economic opportunity, deepened commercial engagement, and long-term mutual prosperity.”

a4373.speaker: JoEllen Gorg, Acting U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4373.name: JoEllen Gorg
a4373.title: Acting U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a4373.speech: Highlighting a strategic shift in U.S. foreign policy, emphasised commercial collaboration: “Under the Trump Administration, the United States is prioritising commercial engagement over development assistance. We want to work with African nations not as aid recipients, but as commercial partners.” ; announced Nigeria’s pivotal role in this new approach, noting, “Nigeria is one of only five African countries that have been selected for this type of agreement,” referring to the U.S.-Nigeria Commercial and Investment Partnership, a five-year initiative that aims to “unlock investment and create well-paying jobs on both sides of the Atlantic” ; celebrated the robust existing ties, revealing, “the two-way trade in goods and services between our nations totalled nearly $13 billion last year, and U.S. foreign direct investment in Nigeria hit $6.5 billion.”

a4373.speaker: Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Lagos State Governor
a4373.name: Babajide Sanwo-Olu
a4373.title: Lagos State Governor
a4373.speech: Echoed the sentiments of partnership, praising the U.S.’s dynamic presence in Lagos: “We have long benefited from the dynamic presence and support of the United States and are especially grateful to the United States Consulate’s investment in young people and ongoing support.” ; “We would like the United States to be even a bigger part of this unfolding story of Lagos and Nigeria.”

a4373.speaker: Dare Art Alade, music artiste
a4373.name: Dare Art Alade
a4373.title: music artiste
a4373.speech: “The democracy that they’re celebrating, we’re fashioning after, and there’s so much synergy between both nations, and that’s what we’re here to celebrate” ; emphasising the vital role of cultural exchange: “Culture is a currency… Let’s bring the authentic stuff from here and show them how it’s done.”

a4373.speaker: Farooq Oreagba, popularly known as King of Steeze
a4373.name: Farooq Oreagba
a4373.title: popularly known as King of Steeze
a4373.speech: Weighed in on the collaboration, acknowledging progress while stressing the need for more: “I think we’re moving in the right direction, but there’s a lot more we can do,” advocating for a stronger Nigerian diplomatic presence globally to secure “fairer deals” ; reiterated Dare’s point: “Culture is a currency… we need to start finding ways where we can collaborate on the culture side.”

a4514.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Somali Prime Minister
a4514.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a4514.title: Somali Prime Minister
a4514.speech: Recently appealed to the Somali diaspora in the United Kingdom to protest outside the British Parliament in a bid to block potential recognition of the breakaway region.

a4514.speaker: Hussein Deyr, Somaliland Presidency Spokesman
a4514.name: Hussein Deyr
a4514.title: Somaliland Presidency Spokesman
a4514.speech: Speaking on Friday, described the Prime Minister's call as a reflection of Mogadishu's frustration, "desperation" and denial of Somaliland's political and "democratic" progress ; "The Somali government is attempting to obscure the reality of Somaliland – a stable, democratic, and self-governing state that has held multiple free and fair elections and maintained peace for decades. These are achievements Somalia has yet to attain," ; reiterated that Somaliland has proven itself to be self-reliant and governed by the rule of law, in stark contrast to what he characterized as widespread violence, corruption, and dependence on foreign aid in Somalia ; "Somaliland's recognition is not merely a plea; it is a reality whose time has come."

a4703.speaker: Ethiopian Constitution of 1923 E.C. (document)
a4703.name: Ethiopian Constitution of 1923 E.C. (document)
a4703.speech: Provided that “the land of Ethiopia, and its people, and its law, in their entirety” belonged to the Emperor.

a4703.speaker: Government of Iraq
a4703.name: Government of Iraq
a4703.speech: Was heard shouting in Tahsas 2008 E.C.: “Turkey has brought her soldiers in without my permission, she has violated my sovereignty…”

a4703.speaker: Some political analysts
a4703.name: Some political analysts
a4703.speech: Have said that sovereignty is a word that ought to be erased from the dictionary.

a4703.speaker: Ruler of Burundi (Pierre Nkurunziza)
a4703.name: Ruler of Burundi (Pierre Nkurunziza)
a4703.speech: Who extended his term of office in 2008 E.C., offered as the reason for his interest in power that he was necessary for the country’s development and for the continuation of democracy.

a4703.speaker: BBC report (2008 E.C.), supported by insider information
a4703.name: BBC report (2008 E.C.)
a4703.title: supported by insider information
a4703.speech: Exposed that the “Islamic” terror state established in Iraq was fundamentally a product of the invasion carried out against Saddam’s Iraq — conceived within the invader’s prison camps and later grown by feeding upon aggrieved Sunnis and upon Saddam’s scattered soldiery.

a4703.speaker: Ethiopian Reporter (editor’s note)
a4703.name: Ethiopian Reporter (editor’s note)
a4703.speech: “We wish to state that the article reflects only the writer’s view.”

a4705.speaker: Suleiman Khalil, official from Syria's transport ministry
a4705.name: Suleiman Khalil
a4705.title: official from Syria's transport ministry
a4705.speech: Told AFP: "Until now 213 planes carrying quake aid have landed in Syria", including 92 from the UAE.

a4705.speaker: Abdul Rahman al-Owais, UAE Health Minister
a4705.name: Abdul Rahman al-Owais
a4705.title: UAE Health Minister
a4705.speech: Told reporters he wished for "a united stance globally to face this huge humanitarian challenge".

a4705.speaker: Joergen Haldorsen, Norwegian Red Cross
a4705.name: Joergen Haldorsen
a4705.title: Norwegian Red Cross
a4705.speech: "Those affected are very vulnerable due to years of war and crisis."

a4705.speaker: European Commission
a4705.name: European Commission
a4705.speech: Encouraged members to respond to Damascus's official plea to the European Union for help.

a4763.speaker: Kabineh M. Ja’nah, former Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Liberia
a4763.name: Kabineh M. Ja’nah
a4763.title: former Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of Liberia
a4763.speech: Says he is mobilizing lawyers to challenge the legality of the 2025 National Budget in court and vows to sue the Government of Liberia, particularly the Executive Branch, if President Joseph N. Boakai signed the controversial Fiscal Year 2025 budget ; speaking on Spoon Midnight conversation, said he has spoken to a few senior lawyers and they are planning that the moment President Boakai signs the Budget, which they believe was passed illegally, they will take the matter to the Supreme Court ; “If the President signed this Budget into law that we believe was not legal at all and didn’t meet the requirements, we will take the government to the Supreme Court to ask for a Legal Declaratory of Properties as to the way this budget was passed. Now, we are not doing this to say oh, this is what we’re going to do to the Supreme Court; we will bring it to the court and say: please make a declaration whether the passage of this budget met the legal requirements under our system” ; said the way they want to do it is by starting from the lower court and after that going to the Supreme Court based on the decision from the lower court, adding that they want the court to clearly state the procedure.

a4763.speaker: J. Fonati Koffa, House Speaker (post on his official Facebook page, 21 December 2024)
a4763.name: J. Fonati Koffa
a4763.title: House Speaker (post on his official Facebook page, 21 December 2024)
a4763.speech: Labels the Majority Bloc’s recent passage of the 2025 national budget as ultra vires – “Ultra vires”.

a4865.speaker: Farhan Jimale, spokesman of the Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia
a4865.name: Farhan Jimale
a4865.title: spokesman of the Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia
a4865.speech: Announced the dismissal of Finance Minister Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur during a mini reshuffle on Saturday night, appointing Bihi Iman Egeh as the new finance minister; the spokesman added that the replacement came after a consultation with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud.

a4865.speaker: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur, Somali Finance Minister (initial suspension letter)
a4865.name: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur
a4865.title: Somali Finance Minister (initial suspension letter)
a4865.speech: Accused Accountant General Mohamed Abdirahman Anas and the Finance Ministry's Director for Revenue, Feisal Mohamed Hashi, of various misconduct, including actions detrimental to national interests, obstruction of the ministry's administration, deliberate payment delays, unwarranted salary withholding, and hindrance to accessing the Somalia Financial Management Information System (SFMIS), a World Bank and IMF-supported financial reporting system.

a4865.speaker: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur, Somali Finance Minister (retraction statement)
a4865.name: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur
a4865.title: Somali Finance Minister (retraction statement)
a4865.speech: Reversed his decision on Friday, stating that the suspensions were lifted but emphasizing that the administrative charges remained, serving as a stern warning for future conduct.

a4865.speaker: Official sources (anonymous)
a4865.name: Official sources (anonymous)
a4865.speech: Revealed that President Mohamud exerted pressure on Minister Nur to rescind the suspensions, as the two officials involved are closely associated with the president.

a4865.speaker: An insider (anonymous)
a4865.name: An insider (anonymous)
a4865.speech: Stated that the sacked officials hold significant responsibility for releasing funds, including kickbacks for the president and his family.

a4865.speaker: Ahmed Ali, political analyst
a4865.name: Ahmed Ali
a4865.title: political analyst
a4865.speech: Criticized the sacking, suggesting that Minister Nur should not have dared to dismiss these influential individuals due to their close ties to powerful figures within the government, including President Mohamud: "For your own survival, you don't touch those connected to the big fish."

a4865.speaker: Ayub Ismail, MP of the Somali Federal Parliament
a4865.name: Ayub Ismail
a4865.title: MP of the Somali Federal Parliament
a4865.speech: Described the situation as a serious matter that affects the entire government, emphasizing the limited power of both the prime minister and the finance minister to fulfill their constitutional duties: "Where the head of government does not have any power to fulfill his constitutional duties, one can imagine how limited the power of the minister is. Therefore, this move is not surprising."

a4865.speaker: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur, dismissed Somali Finance Minister (Facebook post)
a4865.name: Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur
a4865.title: dismissed Somali Finance Minister (Facebook post)
a4865.speech: Expressed his accomplishments during his tenure, highlighting that he ensured timely payment of government employees' salaries and attempted to maintain a non-political approach to financial reforms: "I tried to keep politics out of the financial reform program. I have tried to maintain the institutional system of the Ministry of Finance so that it can efficiently fulfill its mandate, so that we can effectively serve our people."

a4926.speaker: Royal Cabinet of Morocco (communiqué)
a4926.name: Royal Cabinet of Morocco (communiqué)
a4926.speech: Stated that His Majesty Mohammed VI, King of Morocco, held talks at the Royal Palace in Rabat with the President of the French Republic, H.E. Mr Emmanuel Macron, who is making a State Visit to Morocco from 28 to 30 October at the invitation of the Sovereign; that the talks focused on the transition towards a new era of strong relations between Morocco and France within the framework of a renewed Exceptional Partnership and a strategic roadmap for the years to come; that the two Heads of State intend to give decisive impetus to the multidimensional relations of excellence between the two countries; that the talks also covered regional and international issues, with the two Heads of State agreeing to work together to strengthen the Euro-Mediterranean, African and Atlantic projection, and underlining the importance of profoundly renewing the partnership between the two shores of the Mediterranean; and that the President of the French Republic extended an official invitation to His Majesty to make a State Visit to France, which the Sovereign accepted, the date to be agreed through diplomatic channels.

a4926.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of the French Republic
a4926.name: Emmanuel Macron
a4926.title: President of the French Republic
a4926.speech: “I consider that the present and the future of Western Sahara fall within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty. […] For France, autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty is the framework within which this question must be resolved. Our support for the autonomy plan proposed by Morocco in 2007 is clear and constant. For France, it now constitutes the only basis for reaching a just, lasting and negotiated political solution in accordance with the resolutions of the United Nations Security Council” ; hailed the constructive role of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, in the service of peace in the Middle East ; extended an official invitation to His Majesty King Mohammed VI to make a State Visit to France.

a4926.speaker: Declaration on the “Reinforced Exceptional Partnership” between Morocco and France (document)
a4926.name: Declaration on the “Reinforced Exceptional Partnership” between Morocco and France (document)
a4926.speech: Underlines that “The two Heads of State stressed that the ‘Reinforced Exceptional Partnership’ between Morocco and France was intended to be implemented within the broadest possible territorial scope, in the light of the French position expressed on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of His Majesty's accession to the Throne.”

a4926.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and President Emmanuel Macron (joint)
a4926.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and President Emmanuel Macron (joint)
a4926.speech: Called for an immediate cessation of the attacks in Gaza and Lebanon, while stressing the priority of protecting civilian populations and the importance of guaranteeing and facilitating the delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid, while putting an end to the regional conflagration; recalled the urgency of reactivating the peace process, within the framework of the two-State solution, with an independent Palestinian State on the borders of 4 June 1967, with East Jerusalem as its Capital.

a5206.speaker: GDR state press
a5206.name: GDR state press
a5206.speech: Repeats again and again, in large headlines, the message that German fascism arose out of the imperialist stage of capitalism.

a5206.speaker: Official communist historiography (GDR)
a5206.name: Official communist historiography (GDR)
a5206.speech: Describes the battles fought on the German-Soviet front as the decisive ones, and holds that the final victory established a profoundly humane social order over a barbaric imperialist system.

a5206.speaker: American State Department
a5206.name: American State Department
a5206.speech: According to a report by the American State Department, Khmer Rouge troops are carrying out the execution of senior political and military prisoners in Cambodia; the State Department draws this conclusion from a radio broadcast from Cambodia.

a5206.speaker: Henry Kissinger, US Secretary of State
a5206.name: Henry Kissinger
a5206.title: US Secretary of State
a5206.speech: Said in a television interview that it is known that tragic and inhuman things are happening in Cambodia.

a5206.speaker: Max Planck Society
a5206.name: Max Planck Society
a5206.speech: According to the Max Planck Society, animal experiments with dogs showed that even the removal of larger quantities of blood has no adverse consequences; even when the proportion of red blood cells in the test dogs fell to a quarter, there was no danger to life.

a5206.speaker: The scientists (Max Planck Institute for Systems Physiology, Dortmund, and Institute for Surgical Research, Munich)
a5206.name: The scientists (Max Planck Institute for Systems Physiology
a5206.title: Dortmund, and Institute for Surgical Research, Munich)
a5206.speech: Found that in humans the withdrawal of one to at most two litres of blood is normally harmless, but that the procedure can only be used for planned operations where the blood requirement can be estimated in advance.

a5206.speaker: Police reports (Madrid)
a5206.name: Police reports (Madrid)
a5206.speech: Indicate that General Franco would on no account have been injured, even if the parked car had exploded about 100 m from the main entrance of the Bernabeu stadium while the general was passing through the main entrance.

a5230.speaker: Petroineos (operator, company spokesperson)
a5230.name: Petroineos (operator
a5230.title: company spokesperson)
a5230.speech: said Grangemouth, Scotland's only oil refinery, is to close in 2025 with the loss of 400 jobs ; said it was preparing to shut Grangemouth, Britain's oldest refinery, as production ceases in the second quarter of next year, subject to an employee consultation ; cited economic difficulties as the reason for the closure, stating that the company had invested $1.2 billion since 2011, and returned losses in excess of $775 million over the same period ; "Grangemouth is increasingly unable to compete with bigger, more modern and efficient sites in the Middle East, Asia and Africa. Due to its size and configuration, Grangemouth incurs high levels of capital expenditure each year just to maintain its licence to operate" ; said the plant is currently losing around $500,000 per day, and expects to see a $200 million loss for 2024.

a5230.speaker: Reuters
a5230.name: Reuters
a5230.speech: reported that Petroineos was preparing to shut Grangemouth ; further reports that the site will become an import and distribution terminal for finished fuels, which will cut the number of employees at the site from 475 to around 75 over the next two years.

a5230.speaker: Ed Miliband, UK Energy Secretary
a5230.name: Ed Miliband
a5230.title: UK Energy Secretary
a5230.speech: "It is deeply disappointing that Petroineos have confirmed their previous decision to close Grangemouth oil refinery."

a5230.speaker: Analysts
a5230.name: Analysts
a5230.speech: have said the commencement of operation by the Dangote refinery would significantly reduce fuel importation, thereby affecting the businesses of many refineries outside Africa ; anticipate closure of more refineries in Europe if more African countries invest in domestic refining.

a5253.speaker: Ahmed Aden Hameed, Head of the Qatar Red Crescent Office in Somalia
a5253.name: Ahmed Aden Hameed
a5253.title: Head of the Qatar Red Crescent Office in Somalia
a5253.speech: Commended SoDMA for its consistent efforts in addressing humanitarian challenges, reaffirming the organization's commitment to continue supporting development initiatives and providing urgent assistance to vulnerable communities.

a5253.speaker: Mohamud Macalin Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a5253.name: Mohamud Macalin Abdulle
a5253.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a5253.speech: Highlighted the importance of sustained collaboration, stressing that the partnership between the two agencies will help deliver durable and practical solutions to reduce the vulnerability of Somali communities.

a5253.speaker: Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a5253.name: Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a5253.speech: Reiterated its commitment to expanding cooperation with both international and local partners in order to enhance the safety, resilience, and well-being of the Somali people.

a5264.speaker: Michael J. Adler, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.name: Michael J. Adler
a5264.title: U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.speech: Addressing the event, emphasizes the importance of investing in education as a foundational pillar for a country's development, and encouraged the South Sudan government to allocate public revenue transparently and appropriately across all its sectors. "We know this is just a fraction of the millions who need access to these opportunities. Transitional government investment in education is not optional," he said. "It is essential to building a peaceful, prosperous, and self-reliant generation that can help build a better future for this country. So I renew our call in the transitional government to start using public revenue transparently and appropriately to support public education as well as other basic services."

a5264.speaker: Michael J. Adler, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.name: Michael J. Adler
a5264.title: U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.speech: Suggested adequate school funding and timely payment of teachers and lecturers to foster a stable and prosperous future for South Sudanese youth. "Teachers must be paid on time and schools must receive the funding they need to operate. The United States remains committed to helping the people of South Sudan. This commitment is decades old." "It predates the independence of this country. It began and remains based on values, belief in peace, human rights, democracy, and a government responsive to its people's needs." ; Further said the YEA reflects a longstanding commitment from the United States to support the people of South Sudan, rooted in shared values of peace, human rights, democracy, and accountability in governance.

a5264.speaker: Michael J. Adler, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.name: Michael J. Adler
a5264.title: U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan
a5264.speech: Stated that the transitional government's underinvestment in education has prevented millions of youth from accessing essential educational opportunities, and called on government officials to take education responsibility and not depend solely on donor support. "For too long, there has been underinvestment by the transitional government in public education. Millions of South Sudanese youth lack access to the education and opportunities they need to realize their full potential." "Representatives of the ministries, this cannot be left to donors alone to address. The youth empowerment activity is helping by providing foundational literacy and numeracy skills, entrepreneurial training, and knowledge about critical topics."

a5271.speaker: Dr Daniel Siegel, professor of psychology and author of the book The Whole-Brain Child
a5271.name: Dr Daniel Siegel
a5271.title: professor of psychology and author of the book The Whole-Brain Child
a5271.speech: Stresses that when children make mistakes they need to be guided and not punished or shamed. This is where the concept of positive discipline comes in, by teaching children to control their emotions and behaviour in ways that build them up rather than hurt them.

a5271.speaker: Research studies (cited)
a5271.name: Research studies (cited)
a5271.speech: Studies show that caning and shouting often cause fear and a discipline of fear rather than of understanding; these punishments can badly affect a child's mental health and self-confidence, increase aggressive behaviour, reduce the capacity for self-control, and weaken the relationship between parent and child.

a5271.speaker: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP)
a5271.name: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP)
a5271.speech: Has found that physical punishment can build a habit of cruelty in children when they become adults, because they learn to use violence and domination to resolve conflicts and challenges.

a5348.speaker: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) (statement)
a5348.name: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) (statement)
a5348.speech: Warned that the recent decisions by the United States to suspend funding for Ethiopia's national HIV response will be "particularly serious", affecting more than 270,000 beneficiaries in the Oromia and Gambella regions as well as in Addis Ababa ; in a statement released on Thursday said that "the suspension of US assistance to community programmes and drop-in centres serving women, young girls and priority populations at high risk of HIV infection means that tens of thousands of people will no longer be able to access essential services" ; also noted that "the closure of many drop-in centres and the termination of the contracts of outreach workers and peer educators will effectively put an end to support for vulnerable groups."

a5348.speaker: Ethiopian Ministry of Health
a5348.name: Ethiopian Ministry of Health
a5348.speech: Ordered health offices on Wednesday to halt all activities and payments related to employees hired under the US government's budget support, citing the end of USAID funding.

a5348.speaker: USAID
a5348.name: USAID
a5348.speech: Said that the interruption of services in Addis Ababa, Oromia and Gambella will expose 235,560 people to the risk of new HIV infections and sexually transmitted diseases.

a5492.speaker: Dr Vaino Shivute, NIP board deputy chairperson (keynote address)
a5492.name: Dr Vaino Shivute
a5492.title: NIP board deputy chairperson (keynote address)
a5492.speech: "This facility is not just a factory-it is a declaration of Namibia's resolve to dismantle dependency on imports. By producing locally, we safeguard our health sovereignty and ignite economic resilience under Vision 2030 and the Harambee Prosperity Plan II."

a5492.speaker: Neville Andre, Erongo governor
a5492.name: Neville Andre
a5492.title: Erongo governor
a5492.speech: "From eight direct jobs today to over 20 in Phase Two, this hub uplifts families, nurtures skills, and catalyses SMEs in logistics, packaging, and recycling. Erongo's evolution from a logistical gateway to an innovation beacon is unstoppable."

a5492.speaker: Kapena Tjombonde, NIP CEO
a5492.name: Kapena Tjombonde
a5492.title: NIP CEO
a5492.speech: "Through NUST's FabLab, we're moulding futures-training engineers and creating a circular economy. This is how nations leap forward" ; "A single bracelet does not jingle. Together, we ring loud with progress."

a5492.speaker: Dr Iyaloo Konstantinus, NIP Head: Research & Development
a5492.name: Dr Iyaloo Konstantinus
a5492.title: NIP Head: Research & Development
a5492.speech: Emphasised the facility's role in job creation and regional trade.

a5544.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Niger (communiqué)
a5544.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Niger (communiqué)
a5544.speech: Announced on Sunday that the recall of the European Union ambassador in Niamey, Salvador Pinto da França, over the management of funds intended for NGOs to assist flood victims, is “a unilateral initiative of its government and not that of the EU”; indicated that the country “never requested international humanitarian assistance following the floods, and even less so from the EU”, and stressed that the Nigerien government had taken the sovereign decision to finance the repair of flood damage itself.

a5544.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Niger (communiqué)
a5544.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Niger (communiqué)
a5544.speech: Stated that “the announcement of this unrequested aid appeared on social media two weeks before the Nigerien authorities were officially informed, which runs counter to diplomatic usage often recalled by a circular note verbale sent to the diplomatic missions and international organisations accredited in Niger”, adding that “the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation is the sole interlocutor in this matter, implying that even if aid had been requested, it should have gone through this ministry”; said the delivery of this aid to the regions was carried out through NGOs selected by the EU delegation in Niamey, and in “total opacity”; and concluded that, faced with this incident, which “demonstrates a flagrant lack of respect towards the Nigerien authorities”, collaboration with the EU ambassador was no longer conceivable, and it therefore requested his recall and replacement as soon as possible.

a5544.speaker: European Union (communiqué)
a5544.name: European Union (communiqué)
a5544.speech: The EU declared on Saturday, by means of a communiqué, its “disagreement concerning the reasons put forward by Niger regarding the management of humanitarian aid” and had decided to recall its ambassador for consultations.

a5556.speaker: Nelson Mandela
a5556.name: Nelson Mandela
a5556.speech: On 4 October 1996, celebrated South African athletes, calling them "the jewels of the crown" during an official speech.

a5653.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of MCA-Benin
a5653.name: Samuel Batcho
a5653.title: national coordinator of MCA-Benin
a5653.speech: “The Millennium Challenge Corporation gives pride of place to the preservation of the environment, to health, to the safety of populations and to safeguarding the interests of the most vulnerable for all investments made under the Compact.
