That is why the International Finance Corporation's performance standards on environmental and social sustainability must be applied from the design stage through to the full implementation of the Compact.”

a5653.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of MCA-Benin
a5653.name: Samuel Batcho
a5653.title: national coordinator of MCA-Benin
a5653.speech: Said the study of the resettlement framework for the projects of Benin's second Compact will make it possible to “collect data, analyse it and prepare in advance any Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) or, if necessary, livelihood restoration plans and other standard chapters such as the regulatory framework, the institutional framework, the grievance redress mechanism”; and to prepare at least two sets of hypotheses (resettlement scenarios) as well as estimates of the number of people to be displaced for the Energy and Roads projects. He added that the study will allow a better understanding of the activities planned under the next Compact and determine the social costs to be taken into account in defining the projects of the second MCA-Benin programme.

a5653.speaker: Experts present at the workshop
a5653.name: Experts present at the workshop
a5653.speech: Maintained that resettlement may be involuntary when it “refers to any resettlement where expropriation applies while the affected persons do not have the right to refuse”, or voluntary, referring to “any resettlement that is not attributable to expropriation. The operating principles of voluntary resettlement are informed consent and the option to choose.”

a5682.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.name: Bintou Keita
a5682.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.speech: Urged the Security Council on Thursday to concentrate “all efforts towards an unconditional ceasefire” ; recalled that, despite significant regional and international initiatives, the call for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire issued by the East African Community (EAC), SADC, the African Union and Security Council resolution 2773 has still produced no result: “It is imperative that all parties honour their commitment to silence the guns and to seek a peaceful solution.”

a5682.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.name: Bintou Keita
a5682.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.speech: Warned about the security situation: “Today, the AFC/M23 controls vast areas of these provinces and threatens to expand towards Tshopo and Maniema” ; also warned against “the creation of a new politico-military movement, the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP), led by Thomas Lubanga, previously convicted by the International Criminal Court.”

a5682.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.name: Bintou Keita
a5682.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.speech: Stressed that MONUSCO remains “fully committed to fulfilling its mandate” for the protection of civilians: “We have strengthened our cooperation with the local authorities, notably through joint patrols to curb armed criminality.”

a5682.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.name: Bintou Keita
a5682.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General in the DRC
a5682.speech: Denounced “the impact of the prolonged closure of the Goma and Kavumu airports, which hampers the delivery of aid” and called on the Security Council to take concrete measures against the perpetrators of human rights violations and to reopen these essential facilities to facilitate humanitarian aid and the rotation of MONUSCO troops.

a5713.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a5713.name: Elias Magosi
a5713.title: SADC Executive Secretary
a5713.speech: Has called on member states to reduce dependence on foreign aid and embrace regional self-reliance, citing rising geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and a sharp decline in external funding; said the current global climate - marked by tariff hikes and shifting alliances - underscores the urgency for the region to invest in its own resilience. ; "It is becoming increasingly clear to all of us that we stand a better chance when we depend more on our own than on external support, which we have absolutely no control over."

a5713.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a5713.name: Elias Magosi
a5713.title: SADC Executive Secretary
a5713.speech: Urged governments to scale up intra-regional trade, eliminate barriers and invest in infrastructure that accelerates integration; also called for a shift away from exporting raw commodities, noting that manufacturing contributes just 11 percent to SADC's gross domestic product, far below the 30 percent target by 2030.

a5713.speaker: 24th Meeting of the SADC Committee of Ministers of Trade (Harare, June) - resolutions
a5713.name: 24th Meeting of the SADC Committee of Ministers of Trade (Harare
a5713.title: June) - resolutions
a5713.speech: Ministers committed to boosting industrialisation, value addition and regional trade in goods and services.

a5732.speaker: Filippo Grandi, UN High Commissioner for Refugees
a5732.name: Filippo Grandi
a5732.title: UN High Commissioner for Refugees
a5732.speech: Said Mozambique needs to find “the best solutions” for people forced to flee armed attacks in Cabo Delgado and natural calamities, promising support: “The most important thing is how to help the Government find solutions for displaced people, whether helping them to return to their homes or transferring them to other places or [remaining] where they are.” ; “We agree on the next steps and how the United Nations can best assist the central government and local authorities to respond to this situation by providing humanitarian assistance in the short term.” ; added that legal assistance for displaced people and support for their return to areas of origin or definitive resettlement in new areas is planned.

a5732.speaker: Robert Piper, special advisor to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees for Solutions to Internally Displaced Persons
a5732.name: Robert Piper
a5732.title: special advisor to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees for Solutions to Internally Displaced Persons
a5732.speech: Said that Mozambique constitutes a “priority” on the agenda of that United Nations institution, noting that the country faces great needs in terms of humanitarian support: “Mozambique is a priority country for the United Nations, this is a country where we see great needs, hundreds of thousands of Mozambicans have returned to their homes, in recent months, to resume their lives, their subsistence.”

a5732.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) (communiqué)
a5732.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) (communiqué)
a5732.speech: Estimated the number of people who fled terrorist attacks in Cabo Delgado at more than 80,000, asking for food assistance and psychological support: “Six years after the start of the violent conflict in northern Mozambique, people in Cabo Delgado still live in fear. In 2024 alone, more than 80,000 people had to flee following attacks by armed groups” ; “Displaced families urgently need food, shelter, basic necessities and health and mental health care.”

a5732.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) Southern Africa (@MSF_southafrica), social media post
a5732.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) Southern Africa (@MSF_southafrica)
a5732.title: social media post
a5732.speech: “In 2024 alone, over 80,000 people had to flee following attacks by armed groups. The displaced families urgently need food, shelter, relief items, healthcare, and mental healthcare.”

a5732.speaker: Official government data (Mozambique)
a5732.name: Official government data (Mozambique)
a5732.speech: Indicate that the new wave of attacks in recent weeks forced 67,321 people to flee their homelands.

a5732.speaker: Mozambican executive
a5732.name: Mozambican executive
a5732.speech: Justified the incursions as the result of the “movement of small groups of terrorists” who left their bases towards the south of Cabo Delgado, after a period of relative stability.

a5732.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a5732.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a5732.speech: According to UNHCR, the conflict has already displaced one million people.

a5732.speaker: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED)
a5732.name: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED)
a5732.speech: According to ACLED, the conflict has caused around 4,000 deaths.

a5872.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC
a5872.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a5872.title: Director General of Africa CDC
a5872.speech: "Africa cannot continue outsourcing its health security" ; "This strategy is not about aid-it's about ownership. We are building a future where Africa invests in its people, drives its own health agenda, and responds to crises with speed, strength, and self-reliance."

a5872.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a5872.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a5872.speech: Launched a continent-wide strategy aimed at transforming how health systems are financed; the strategy urges governments to fulfil the Abuja Declaration by allocating at least 15% of national budgets to health, introduces innovative financing ideas such as solidarity levies on airline tickets, alcohol, and mobile services, and explores how Africa's US$95 billion in annual diaspora remittances can support national health priorities ; according to the Africa CDC, implementation will be phased, with the first phase (2025-2026) focused on updating national health financing plans in 30 countries, piloting innovative revenue mechanisms, and launching transparency dashboards, and the second phase (2026-2030) scaling successful approaches to enable at least 20 countries to finance 50 percent or more of their health budgets through sustainable domestic sources.

a5872.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC
a5872.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a5872.title: Director General of Africa CDC
a5872.speech: Says they will deploy a new African Health Financing Scorecard to monitor progress, improve donor alignment, and boost efficiency in domestic spending.

a5918.speaker: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5918.name: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5918.speech: Says a decision on Liberia's continued eligibility for a second Compact will be made in December this year; at the meeting held on August 21, 2025, after discussing the results of the Foreign Assistance Review conducted by the U.S. State Department, the Board decided that the decision will be made in December 2025 during the MCC regular Board meeting.

a5918.speaker: Jason Small, MCC Acting Vice President for the Department of Compact Operations (letter of August 22, 2025)
a5918.name: Jason Small
a5918.title: MCC Acting Vice President for the Department of Compact Operations (letter of August 22, 2025)
a5918.speech: Informed Liberia's Minister of Finance & Development Planning that MCC's continuing engagement on development of a Compact with Liberia will focus on areas that can inform the Board's December deliberations: “As a next step, MCC will work with you to identify sectors that a Compact could focus on to support economic growth in Liberia while offering opportunities for U.S. business engagements and other mutual benefits.” ; Informed Minister Ngafuan that the “MCC intends to send a team to Liberia to advance these discussions at a time that is mutually convenient,” saying “Our team will be in touch with further details.” ; Thanked Minister Ngafuan for visiting MCC Headquarters in July 2025 and for the strong partnership, stressing that MCC is proud of the work accomplished together through the first MCC compact with Liberia.

a5918.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance & Development Planning
a5918.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5918.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance & Development Planning
a5918.speech: Thanked Mr Small for the update and extended President Boakai and the Liberian government's deep appreciation to the MCC Management and the U.S. government for the strong support to Liberia's development; heartily welcomed the MCC's decision to field a team to Liberia to identify sectors that could benefit from MCC support through a possible second Compact, and informed Mr Small that the Liberian government avidly anticipates the visit of the MCC team in the shortest possible time.

a5981.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a5981.name: United Nations (UN)
a5981.speech: Has urged Malawi to do more in expanding domestic financing for development, saying “it cannot be business as usual” in the face of emerging aid cuts.

a5981.speaker: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh, UN resident coordinator in Malawi
a5981.name: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh
a5981.title: UN resident coordinator in Malawi
a5981.speech: Made the call in Lilongwe during the launch of the Integrated National Financing Framework (INFF) and the Malawi SDG Investor Map; said there is a need for more innovative and practical solutions to bridge the financing gap, and cited the Addis Ababa Action Agenda which encourages governments, international organisations, the private sector and civil society to do more to increase financial resources for sustainable development ; “The global development financing landscape is facing significant headwinds, marked by recent policy shifts and aid cuts. This amplifies the need for developing countries, like Malawi, to do more in expanding domestic financing for development.”

a5981.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, European Union Ambassador to Malawi
a5981.name: Rune Skinnebach
a5981.title: European Union Ambassador to Malawi
a5981.speech: Urged the country to overtake regional competitors by implementing policy commitments; said there is huge commitment for investment while urging Malawi government’s commitment to private sector development to be stronger than that of neighbouring countries ; “It is not enough to create a predictable and secure investment climate. We also need to create an investment climate which is more attractive than neighbouring countries.”

a5981.speaker: Firas Raad, World Bank country manager
a5981.name: Firas Raad
a5981.title: World Bank country manager
a5981.speech: Painted a positive picture for Malawi, saying the challenges facing Malawi are not invincible; advised that it will take a lot of work to achieve Malawi 2063 targets for 2030 and 2063, observing that modernisation takes decades of sustained reforms ; “Malawi can take heart that many countries have been able to make the transition from low income to middle income and then upper income to high income.”

a5981.speaker: Simplex Chithola Banda, Minister of Finance
a5981.name: Simplex Chithola Banda
a5981.title: Minister of Finance
a5981.speech: Advised government agencies to integrate the INFF into their planning while urging the private sector to explore the Investor Map and create solutions.

a5981.speaker: Joseph Nagoli, National Planning Commission acting director general
a5981.name: Joseph Nagoli
a5981.title: National Planning Commission acting director general
a5981.speech: Said the two documents are detailing how the country can finance its development as part of accelerating the development trajectory; noted that Malawi needs to look beyond the national budget in financing development, saying financing can be through public private partnerships for example in road infrastructure ; “We cannot only rely on the national budget for development. We need alternative financing and that is why we have the two documents. Fiscal space for development is very small so we cannot rely on the 20 percent development to develop this country.”

a6059.speaker: World Bank (data)
a6059.name: World Bank (data)
a6059.speech: According to World Bank data, the growth rate was 9.06% in 1962, then reached 21.33% in 1970, before dropping drastically with the 1972 crisis to -6.4%.

a6059.speaker: E. N., former employee of Cogerco
a6059.name: E. N.
a6059.title: former employee of Cogerco
a6059.speech: recalls: “The cotton plantations covered almost the entire plain and, to kill the insects, an aeroplane was used. In fact, Cotebu’s fibres were well regarded in the region.” According to him, production was good, and with Cotebu the uniforms of the gendarmes, schoolchildren and soldiers were produced locally. “That no doubt allowed the country to save foreign currency,” adds this man in his sixties.

a6059.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi
a6059.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a6059.title: President of Burundi
a6059.speech: organised, in November 2021, the National Development Forum to make Burundi “an emerging country by 2040”.

a6059.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, National Director of PARCEM
a6059.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a6059.title: National Director of PARCEM
a6059.speech: paints a bleak picture of 60 years of independence: “60 years of independence, advances but also setbacks”. The country’s economic situation has evolved decrescendo from 1962 to today. Looking at income per capita, the growth rate and the production of certain export crops, notably coffee, we are at a much lower level. We are the poorest country in the world, with a GDP per capita of less than 300 dollars. Burundians numbered 2 million in 1962; today we are 12 million, while GDP has not increased in the same proportions.

a6059.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, National Director of PARCEM
a6059.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a6059.title: National Director of PARCEM
a6059.speech: said both endogenous and exogenous factors explain the situation: notably the political crises that weighed heavily on the country’s economy — with the 1972 crisis GDP fell by 6%, and during the 1993-2005 crisis GDP contracted by 33% — and exogenous factors such as the World Bank’s structural adjustment programme, which left the country unable to continue on the same investment momentum.

a6059.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, National Director of PARCEM
a6059.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a6059.title: National Director of PARCEM
a6059.speech: said on shortages of basic goods and untimely power cuts that the lack of a business environment means the country stays with the same firms despite demographic pressure, and that corruption and economic malpractice prevent industries from increasing their production capacity to meet demand.

a6059.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, National Director of PARCEM
a6059.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a6059.title: National Director of PARCEM
a6059.speech: said there is reason to hope for change through the lifting of Brussels’ sanctions and the international opening of the Ndayishimiye regime, but the administrative apparatus does not show the same enthusiasm despite the president’s speeches; the reforms initiated by President Ndayishimiye are sometimes blocked by regime dignitaries who feel threatened, and the president must break these pockets of resistance to his programme in order to move forward.

a6222.speaker: U.S. Government
a6222.name: U.S. Government
a6222.speech: Considers the Matola Santos Hospital to be a critical investment that will improve the country's ability to control the national HIV epidemic and respond independently to other disease threats.

a6222.speaker: U.S. Government
a6222.name: U.S. Government
a6222.speech: Has pledged approximately $3.6 million to fund health facility renovations, SAAJs (school health centers), and a new molecular biology laboratory in Gaza Province in 2020.

a6222.speaker: Current HIV treatment data (Mozambique/PEPFAR figures cited)
a6222.name: Current HIV treatment data (Mozambique/PEPFAR figures cited)
a6222.speech: Current data reflects the impact of the HIV epidemic in Matola and the need for comprehensive care and treatment. In July 2020, 143,873 people were in HIV treatment in Maputo Province, 64,871 of whom were in the district of Matola, and 7,265 of whom were seen at Matola Health Center C and Matola Santos Mobile Clinic with clinical technical assistance from Ariel Glaser Foundation Against Pediatric AIDS (ARIEL).

a6511.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6511.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6511.speech: Has announced that delegates from all 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory will convene in Lagos next month for the 7th National Council on AIDS (NCA), themed “Advancing National HIV Sustainability Agenda in the Changing Global Policy on Aid.”

a6511.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA and Chair of the Council
a6511.name: Temitope Ilori
a6511.title: Director-General of NACA and Chair of the Council
a6511.speech: In a statement issued on Thursday, highlighted the urgency of national ownership and emphasised the need for Nigeria to take greater responsibility for its HIV response as donor support continues to decline: “As donor landscapes evolve, Nigeria must take bold steps to ensure that HIV prevention, treatment, and support remain accessible and resilient. The Council offers us a unified platform to chart that future.”

a6511.speaker: NACA (statement)
a6511.name: NACA (statement)
a6511.speech: According to the statement, three thematic areas will guide this year's discussions: advancing the national HIV sustainability agenda within a changing global aid landscape; adopting multi-sectoral approaches to HIV and related diseases; and strengthening sub-national structures to improve health system resilience. NACA said the meeting is not only strategic for evaluating past progress but also critical for aligning efforts across sectors such as tuberculosis, malaria, reproductive health, and other development priorities.

a6588.speaker: German Embassy in Mozambique (press release)
a6588.name: German Embassy in Mozambique (press release)
a6588.speech: States that cooperation between Mozambique and Germany has reached more than 1.8 billion euros over the past 40 years and that the current value of projects under implementation totals about 850 million euros.

a6588.speaker: Ronald Münch, German Ambassador to Mozambique
a6588.name: Ronald Münch
a6588.title: German Ambassador to Mozambique
a6588.speech: Acknowledged the lasting impact that German development aid has had on Mozambicans, pointing to examples of the contribution to job creation, increased access to electricity and the strengthening of vocational training; according to Münch, the cooperation "provided access to financial services for hundreds of thousands of people. The exhibition highlighted those results."

a7044.speaker: Alemnesh Neri, 43-year-old traveller from Gumer
a7044.name: Alemnesh Neri
a7044.title: 43-year-old traveller from Gumer
a7044.speech: “From spices to clothing, these stops offer a break from rising city prices. But, the journey has turned into a race against time.” ; “This is home. No matter the challenges, it's where my heart is.”

a7044.speaker: A tour operator (unnamed)
a7044.name: A tour operator (unnamed)
a7044.speech: “Safety has become a paramount concern. The risks have led many to reconsider their travel plans.”

a7044.speaker: Getu Yilma, tourist visiting from Johannesburg, South Africa
a7044.name: Getu Yilma
a7044.title: tourist visiting from Johannesburg, South Africa
a7044.speech: Acknowledged the progress and the persistent problems in the region's tourism development: “The zone needs to have better roads. Improvements to local infrastructure could enhance the tourism experience.” ; “It's a connection to our heritage that keeps us coming back.”

a7044.speaker: Bogale Abey, owner of Dynasty Ethiopia Tour
a7044.name: Bogale Abey
a7044.title: owner of Dynasty Ethiopia Tour
a7044.speech: “Tourists cannot obtain travel insurance with a travel advisory against the country of destination.”

a7044.speaker: Ftsum Gezahegn, president of the Ethiopian Tour Operators Association
a7044.name: Ftsum Gezahegn
a7044.title: president of the Ethiopian Tour Operators Association
a7044.speech: Said improved marketing and promotion of Ethiopia, as well as streamlined visa processes, are needed to attract more international visitors: “We've so much to offer, but the obstacles are formidable.”

a7044.speaker: Ftsum Gezahegn, president of the Ethiopian Tour Operators Association
a7044.name: Ftsum Gezahegn
a7044.title: president of the Ethiopian Tour Operators Association
a7044.speech: Concurred with the call for increased state support, saying that while laws permit tour operators to import vehicles tax-free, more needs to be done, particularly in addressing security concerns: “We need loans and tax incentives for operators to help the sector recover.”

a7044.speaker: Henok Seyoum, travel journalist
a7044.name: Henok Seyoum
a7044.title: travel journalist
a7044.speech: Observed a near complete absence of foreign tourists in his tours of southern Ethiopia this September, citing ongoing regional security concerns and limited local movement, and said substantial incentives and investments for service providers in the sector are crucial, noting that tour operators pay VAT even though most of their expenses are not issued with receipts and thus cannot claim rebates: “The financial burden on operators is unsustainable.”

a7044.speaker: Meseret Amelga, head of the Gurage Zone Culture & Tourism Bureau
a7044.name: Meseret Amelga
a7044.title: head of the Gurage Zone Culture & Tourism Bureau
a7044.speech: Said the Zonal office expected to generate more than 100 million Br in transactions during the season, with officials anticipating more than 800,000 visitors this holiday season, including 3,000 foreign tourists, a projected 40pc increase from the previous year.

a7044.speaker: Meseret Amelga, head of the Gurage Zone Culture & Tourism Bureau
a7044.name: Meseret Amelga
a7044.title: head of the Gurage Zone Culture & Tourism Bureau
a7044.speech: Acknowledged that the region still suffers from manifold constraints, particularly of infrastructure: “Local roads remain underdeveloped, and improvements to basic services such as water and electricity are urgently needed to sustain long-term tourism growth.”

a7044.speaker: Ashenafi Mulugeta, president of the Addis Abeba Hotel & Tourism Professionals' Association
a7044.name: Ashenafi Mulugeta
a7044.title: president of the Addis Abeba Hotel & Tourism Professionals' Association
a7044.speech: “More than 150 hotels in the city were ready to serve tourists arriving for the ceremonies.”

a7044.speaker: Ministry of Tourism (data)
a7044.name: Ministry of Tourism (data)
a7044.speech: Data from the Ministry of Tourism show that Ethiopia generated 4.3 billion dollars in tourism revenue from 1.1 million visitors last year.

a7044.speaker: Ministry of Tourism officials
a7044.name: Ministry of Tourism officials
a7044.speech: Plan to draw 200,000 more tourists this year, including 395,218 during the peak season from September to December, hoping to generate 5.47 billion dollars.

a7044.speaker: Atlaw Alemu (PhD), Addis Abeba University
a7044.name: Atlaw Alemu (PhD)
a7044.title: Addis Abeba University
a7044.speech: Argued that the extremely low tourist visibility contradicts the Ministry's reported income, especially considering the widespread closure of tourist destinations: “The Covid-19 pandemic's effects on the tourism sector require in-depth analysis to identify areas needing greater focus. We can't say we have tourists when there are just a few.”

a7110.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a7110.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a7110.title: President of Zimbabwe
a7110.speech: Said that despite the challenges posed by the illegal sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe by hostile Western nations, Zimbabwe remains committed to multilateralism and international cooperation to help realise global peace, security, justice, and equitable development: "Our doors are open and our hands remain outstretched to all nations, private sector stakeholders, and development partners. We stand ready to welcome those willing to work with us, as we build stronger, win-win partnerships and synergies, for shared prosperity and lasting development." ; "As a progressive member of the international community, we will continuously lend our voice and efforts in addressing threats to global peace and stability. Hence, Zimbabwe has presented its candidature for a non-permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council for the term 2027 to 2028."

a7110.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a7110.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a7110.title: President of Zimbabwe
a7110.speech: Added that Zimbabwe recognises the potential of heritage-based innovation and production as a catalyst for value addition, beneficiation and inclusive economic growth, and that the Government is implementing targeted initiatives to empower communities so that they leverage and tap into their respective comparative advantages to meet global demand for unique and authentic Zimbabwean products: "It is a befitting reminder of the value of heritage-based innovation as our national development blueprint for broad, inclusive growth, dignity, and self-determination. In this regard, marketing authorities have scaled up the promotion of the export of goods, services, and minerals, among others. These are rooted in our cultural identity and indigenous knowledge systems, including traditional foods, arts, crafts, and culture."

a7110.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a7110.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a7110.title: President of Zimbabwe
a7110.speech: "In navigating the path towards sustainable economic development, Zimbabwe, like other developing countries, recognises the critical importance of access to flexible and reliable lines of credit. Regrettably, the illegal economic sanctions have fundamentally disrupted the ability of our country to access global lines of credit," ; added that to ensure the continuity of the developmental agenda, the Government has adopted home-grown innovative development financing models to drive the country forward ; "Similarly, the implementation of political and legislative reforms that benefit the people is ongoing and entrenching Zimbabwe's standing as a constitutional democracy. Through modernising and industrialising our economy, as well as shaping our own narratives, we are demonstrating that locally driven progress can never be sanctioned or delayed."

a7360.speaker: Daouda Simboro, Director General of the Banque agricole du Faso (BADF)
a7360.name: Daouda Simboro
a7360.title: Director General of the Banque agricole du Faso (BADF)
a7360.speech: Said the BADF is a bank whose core business is the financing of agriculture but also a modern bank financing any activity contributing to the growth of the Burkinabe economy; that it is a source of pride that this bank is the fruit of national expertise with exclusively Burkinabe capital; and that the BADF positions itself as a bank close to its clients, accessible to all, with as its major objective the satisfaction of their needs.

a7360.speaker: Daouda Simboro, Director General of the Banque agricole du Faso (BADF)
a7360.name: Daouda Simboro
a7360.title: Director General of the Banque agricole du Faso (BADF)
a7360.speech: "The BADF has resolutely turned towards the extension of its network by opening, almost at a run, within the space of two years, five branches, two of them in Ouagadougou and one in each of the cities of Bobo-Dioulasso, Dedougou and Hounde." ; Assured that before the end of 2021 the bank will open its doors to the populations of Diebougou, Kaya and Bagre, and indicated that since its launch in March 2019 his institution has granted "several" tens of billions of CFA francs in credit to the national economy.

a7360.speaker: Madou Hema, President of the Cascades consular delegation of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Burkina Faso (CCI-BF), Chairman and CEO of Borondo SARL and patron of the ceremony
a7360.name: Madou Hema
a7360.title: President of the Cascades consular delegation of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Burkina Faso (CCI-BF), Chairman and CEO of Borondo SARL and patron of the ceremony
a7360.speech: Said the BADF was created on the foundation of the express demand of the rural world and of the will of the country's highest authorities ; "The opening of a branch in the city of Banfora today is both a feat and a measure of the economic reach of the city, of the whole region and its surroundings."

a7360.speaker: Madou Hema, President of the Cascades consular delegation of the CCI-BF and patron of the ceremony
a7360.name: Madou Hema
a7360.title: President of the Cascades consular delegation of the CCI-BF and patron of the ceremony
a7360.speech: Said that if the BADF confined itself solely to financing agro-sylvo-pastoral, wildlife and fisheries production activities while setting aside other sectors such as transport, processing, roads, trade, businesses and health infrastructure, it would have done unfinished work ; urged his godchildren "to translate" the bank's "noble vision" "vividly into facts".

a7360.speaker: Bakanhaye Hema, chief of staff of the mayor of Banfora, representing the mayor
a7360.name: Bakanhaye Hema
a7360.title: chief of staff of the mayor of Banfora, representing the mayor
a7360.speech: Asked the Banque agricole du Faso to be a "genuine" tool at the service of local development.

a7360.speaker: Mahamad Michara, Secretary General of the Cascades region, representing the governor
a7360.name: Mahamad Michara
a7360.title: Secretary General of the Cascades region, representing the governor
a7360.speech: "In the field of agriculture, many things need to be reviewed, rehabilitated and reinvented, including the methods of financing and of organisation, hence the need for farmers to have a bank they can turn to." ; Said this bank is the one that "speaks their language, that understands their constraints, that looks a little further than their borrower profile and that offers them easy access and various quality services for better yields", and urged the BADF to amplify its financing and to propose innovative products in favour of a more dynamic rural world.

a7470.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7470.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7470.title: President of Ghana
a7470.speech: Highlighted the pressing need for reforms within international institutions, particularly in light of the disruption caused by the Trump administration's cuts to USAID funding: “Before I boarded the flight to come to Munich, I issued a directive to our Minister of Finance to make adjustments in our budgets to take up the slack” ; emphasised that the funds are critical for governance, healthcare, economic growth, and education in Africa.

a7470.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7470.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7470.title: President of Ghana
a7470.speech: Called for reforms at the United Nations, stating: “We will not have the luxury to double or triple parallel activities inside the UN system. There is a need to sit together, to work together.”
